Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”.

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the upcoming format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

#176746. Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1038 w)

Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • It has been revealed that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

It has been revealed that the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

In a recent development, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

Industry observers note that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," stated Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

"There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

It has been revealed that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

Sources indicate that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

According to recent reports, in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she mentioned.

Industry observers note that "It is isolated," she stated. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she stated.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

Industry observers note that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

"We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin noted. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

Sources indicate that it's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, stated R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

"That's when spreads really widen out," he mentioned. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

Why Portable Medical Technology Needs More Than Portability

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • ​Making a medical device smaller changes where it can go, but it takes more than portability to bring that technology into a upcoming care setting.
  • According to recent reports, primary care offices, wound clinics, ambulances and patients’ homes, and the people using medical devices in those settings, have different needs than a specialist department.
  • Sources indicate that the opportunity for developers is not simply to move existing equipment into latest locations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aaron Timm is the CEO of Openwater.

​Making a medical device smaller changes where it can go, but it takes more than portability to bring that technology into a upcoming care setting. It requires understanding who will operate it, what clinical need it addresses and how it fits into the delivery of care. Advances in hardware, software and AI are creating new possibilities, carrying advanced technology into places it rarely reached before. But portability alone does not ensure adoption.​.

According to recent reports, primary care offices, wound clinics, ambulances and patients’ homes, and the people using medical devices in those settings, have different needs than a specialist department. These settings may offer less time for testing, fewer staff with device-specific training and tighter budgets. Users need information they can act on within those constraints.

Sources indicate that the opportunity for developers is not simply to move existing equipment into latest locations. Engaging care providers in new settings requires designing technology around those settings from the start. For example, what information or intervention does the clinician need? Who will operate the device? What happens after a result is available? Those questions should shape product development as much as size, cost or technical performance.​.

It has been revealed that A growing number of devices, both on the market and in development, illustrate how technology can be adapted to different consumers and care settings. For example, researchers are studying a portable, wearable device that uses light to measure blood flow in the brain to help ambulance crews identify the most severe strokes. In an early study, it detected large vessel occlusions more reliably than the symptom checklists that paramedics typically use.

In a recent development, portability also matters for inpatient care, because it allows clinicians to bring the technology directly to patients who may be too unstable to move. One study of portable, low-field MRI in 50 critically ill patients demonstrated the feasibility of bedside scanning, with no adverse events reported, showing how inpatient settings stand to gain from advancements in medical device tech. ​.

According to recent reports, outside the hospital, advanced diagnostics are reaching primary care offices and even patients’ homes. An AI-based eye exam allows primary care practices to screen patients with diabetes for eye damage without an eye specialist reading the images. In the study behind its FDA authorization, office staff were capable of running the tests after about four hours of training.

Older adults with a common form of age-related vision loss can also now scan their own eyes at home with results available for remote review by their treating physician. These examples address different barriers to access: where a test can be performed, who can perform it and how results reach the clinician responsible for follow-up. Manufacturers need to identify which barrier they are solving, rather than treating portability as the solution to all three.​.

According to recent reports, while advances in technology are largely responsible for bringing advanced devices to the point of care, healthcare policies and workforce needs add to the growing momentum. Earlier this year, Congress extended Medicare’s hospital-at-home program through 2030, and hundreds of programs across dozens of states have been approved to provide hospital-level care in patients’ homes.

One industry forecast projects that home-based care, outpatient services and clinics will see the fastest volume increases of any care setting over the next decade, signaling a need for more portable, low-cost technologies that require fewer specialists to operate them or interpret results.

The workforce and payment aspects of care appear to be moving in a similar direction. In radiology, for example, workforce researchers project that the supply of specialists will grow at roughly the same rate as demand for imaging over the next three decades, meaning the current shortage is unlikely to improve without changes in how imaging is delivered.

Sources indicate that payers, meanwhile, have started to recognize imaging done outside traditional settings. For manufacturers, the practical question is whether a device has a workable payment model or creates enough operational value to justify its full cost, including staff time, training and follow-up. Billing codes also now exist for the remote review of home eye scans mentioned above, showing a willingness from payers to consider nontraditional imaging.

In a recent development, with specialists in short supply and payers more open to new models, the decision to buy advanced medical technology is expanding to include the departments that will act on its results, such as emergency medicine, primary care and home health programs. For these buyers, technical performance is only the starting point.

Recent findings suggest that they also need to know how much training staff will require, whether the evidence reflects the intended people and setting, how the device fits into daily routines and whether reimbursement or operational savings justify the full cost of using it. Manufacturers now have the opportunity to reach a new category of buyers by going beyond portability, making the technology practical for the team that will use it.​.

He was Vlada Djuric, a 50-year-old Macedonian of Romani descent and part of the wider Nikolov family, including his wife Zora Jovanovic, their two sons and daughter, whose highly organised thefts from the homes of top footballers would continue for more than a decade, with imprisonment deemed only a minor setback.

While the Nainggolans were blithely unaware of the criminal family’s lookout man – they’d gone to visit friends nearby for a couple of hours and hadn't even bothered to activate the burglar alarm – the assailants were primed to seize the chance.

The two sons, Valentino and Giacomo, mounted the villa’s perimeter wall, opening one door with a magnetic card and jimmying another with a screwdriver, and proceeded undisturbed through the house in 27 minutes, throwing the proceeds of their burglary into a bag as they went.

Recent findings suggest that there were 15 watches (Rolex, Patek Philippe and others) valued at £250,000 and 20 pieces of jewellery, including a diamond worth £25,000. Security cameras on a landing and in an internal room filmed them but such was their confidence, they only partially covered their faces.

Former Roma midfielder Radja Nainggolan and his then wife Claudia, who was six months pregnant, were the targets of a burglary in 2016 (Source: Instagram/Claudia_lai_82).

Nainggolan had an extraordinary £400,000 worth of possessions taken, including 15 watches.

The watches matched the descriptions of those stolen from the Nainggolans, though it was a necklace with a Roma logo, and the pair of red shoes with Nainggolan's initials, which really gave the game away.

Sources indicate that ‘I ask again for vigilance and watchfulness, please,’ Failla stated at the time, because this was the fourth time that footballers' properties in Casal Palocco had been targeted in the space of five years. But the challenge of placing footballers in a state of constant vigilance became clear fully seven years on, when another Nainggolan residence, in Antwerp, Belgium, was burgled while his relatives held a party there.

In a recent development, ‘It is one of the most complicated and consistently challenging parts of our security work,’ one former special forces soldier now providing security for footballers tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘It’s been a big sector of our work for years now, but the movements of these clients are so public and that’s irresistible to criminals. Paul Hughes, managing director of Benchmark Security Group, a leading Manchester-based protection firm, employs former police and Royal security drivers to train his clients in the art of 'defensive driving'.

In a two-hour session, they learn how to avoid being 'boxed in' – as Ozil and Kolasinac were – when approaching traffic lights. Techniques include never taking up a position in the middle lane, avoiding the outside lane if there is a central barrier, and always maintaining sight of the tyres of the vehicle in front when you slow.

'If you can see the tyres, you will always have room to manoeuvre right or left of the car in front, at speed, without hitting it,' Hughes notes.

In a recent development, his staff are often asked to escort clients in their fleet of vehicles, which includes two Land Rovers with blacked-out windows. The firm acquired a Darkfighter Dome – a night-vision camera which is mounted on to the roof of its security vehicles – allowing them to see would-be assailants in the dark. Escorted school runs are also part of the protection they offer.

A screen which dominates Benchmark's underground headquarters, at anonymous premises in Manchester, revealed the fortresses that players' houses have become, when I visited.

Sources indicate that it indicated live feeds from the gardens of mansions which are criss-crossed by infra-red beams. An alarm is triggered in the control room if anyone not approved through face-recognition software is picked up by up to 18 pan, tilt and zoom cameras at a property.

Loudspeakers, operated from the control room, warn off intruders. A team of security staff is never more than six minutes away. A patrol is on the scene of an alert, usually within 90 seconds.

A number of Manchester United players have invested in specialised security dogs from the Leicester-based firm Chaperone K9 at a cost of up to £20,000 each, though some sources suggest demand has receded as many players have young children. Security firms have their own dogs.

In a recent development, benchmark are one of Britain's most trusted operators – industry-accredited, with former senior police officers on their staff. But this is also a world in which some unsavoury individuals are looking to extract gain.

Daily Mail Sport is aware that a number of current players have paid protection money to ensure they remain safe and are not venturing out socially without having done so. The ‘panic rooms’ some install in their homes, with security card access, are a place to hide valuables.

The family who preyed on footballers for a decade will be behind bars for some time. Valentino Nikolov (pictured) is serving an initial 10-year sentence, which has since been extended.

Kolasinac fought off the carjackers. Everton's Duncan Ferguson put an assailant in hospital when he tried to burgle his home at Ormskirk, Lancashire, in January 2001. ‘I’m not a hard man off the pitch...unless you try to break into my house,’ he said recently.

But the assailants in the Ozil and Kolasinac attack were part of Eastern European gangs. 'The criminal demographic has changed,' one former senior detective tells me. 'We are now talking about gangs who lack the slightest compunction about taking a life.'.

Strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

According to recent reports, we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three major inflation measures to be released. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI indicated wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

Predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Sources indicate that markets are presently anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

#176739. ​Should You Trust AI? You Need To Understand The Work First

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (827 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

​Should You Trust AI? You Need To Understand The Work First

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (827 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Vibe coding” has brought new attention to an already controversial topic: Should you trust AI with your work?
  • In my experience, what separates the two often comes down to the person directing the agent: their understanding of the work, the technology and the limitations of the approach they have chosen.
  • It has been revealed that responsible AI use requires two kinds of competence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patrick Dajos - Founding Team at Hyperbound.

“Vibe coding” has brought new attention to an already controversial topic: Should you trust AI with your work? I have seen both terrible and exceptionally good results produced with AI.

In my experience, what separates the two often comes down to the person directing the agent: their understanding of the work, the technology and the limitations of the approach they have chosen.

It has been revealed that responsible AI use requires two kinds of competence. You need to understand what the agent produces and why it works. You also need enough technical knowledge to recognize when its approach is failing and identify a better one. Both matter when you are accountable for the result.

Recent findings suggest that I treat my AI agent like a coworker. I explain the assignment, provide context and review the work. Effective delegation depends on knowing which responsibilities it can handle, what information it needs and where I will need to intervene.

With software, reviewing the visible result is insufficient. A feature can behave correctly in a demonstration while mishandling permissions, losing data under certain conditions or introducing a dependency the team cannot maintain.

Recent findings suggest that before approving a change, I should be able to explain what was generated, how it works and why the approach is appropriate. That includes understanding how it fits the existing system and which assumptions its correctness depends on.

In a recent development, an agent’s explanation can help me investigate those questions. It cannot substitute for checking the implementation. If I accept its account without comparing it with the code and observed behavior, I am trusting another generated answer.

Sources indicate that A practical review should establish what changed, what was tested, which failure cases were considered and what remains unverified. The reviewer then needs to check the consequential claims. I need enough understanding to defend the decision and help resolve a problem if it fails.

Technical understanding also determines how effectively you can direct an agent before there is anything to approve. I encountered this when I asked Codex to create motion graphics for marketing. It generated images using an AI image model and animated them in After Effects. It completed the assignment, but the result was underwhelming. It looked like the “AI slop” I wanted to avoid.

In a recent development, having worked with computer graphics, I knew there was another way: I could show AI examples of what I wanted and ask it to write the instructions that tell the computer what to draw as the animation plays. Those instructions are called shaders. Writing code is one of AI’s strengths, and once I gave it that job, it produced an animation we could actually use.​.

Recent findings suggest that that experience illustrates why knowing how to ask for something is only part of using AI well. You need to understand the available methods, recognize their limitations and identify which approach gives the agent a better chance of meeting the requirement. Without that knowledge, you may keep requesting improvements within a method that is poorly suited to the task.

The same judgment applies in software development. When an implementation repeatedly fails, you need to assess whether the problem lies in the requirements, the available context or the design itself. Each diagnosis calls for a different intervention.

Sources indicate that this places a responsibility on the user to recognize their own limitations. If I cannot assess an approach or explain its output, I need to address that gap before relying on the result.

According to recent reports, AI can be exceptionally useful for doing exactly that. It can help research an unfamiliar subject, compare methods and explain a mechanism through successive examples. I can question an explanation, ask what would make an approach fail and work through the parts I do not understand.

In a recent development, the test is whether I can then reason about the decision myself. Can I explain its tradeoffs? Can I recognize a situation in which another approach would be better? Important claims still need verification against reliable sources.

Industry observers note that nobody needs to master every specialty, but consequential technical work needs someone qualified to assess it. When my understanding is insufficient, I need to learn more or involve someone with the relevant expertise.

In a recent development, for technology leaders, these competencies should shape how AI is introduced into a team. Faster output has value when people can choose an appropriate method, evaluate the implementation and support the finished work.

Industry observers note that AI can perform a substantial share of the execution. The person approving it remains responsible for knowing what they are accepting and why it deserves their confidence. If the work goes out under my name, I need to be able to stand behind it.​.

Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

According to recent reports, eli Lilly (LLY +2.94%) continues to crush it, thanks to the success of its existing portfolio of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. But with its drug candidate Retatrutide, a "triple agonist" that mimics three key gut hormones, the pharmaceutical firm may have an opportunity to market it as a treatment for another common ailment: obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

At least, that's an emerging takeaway, following the publication of recent phase 3 trial results in the Newly introduced England Journal of Medicine. OSA affects over 50 million Americans, with an estimated 80% unaware they have the disorder. Hence, there is tremendous financial opportunity for products targeting it.

In a recent development, two separate clinical trials, one for patients with type 2 diabetes and one for patients who do not have type 2 diabetes, demonstrated how weekly injections of Retatrutide significantly reduced their symptoms. Depending on the dosage, the treatment reduced OSA "episodes" by up to 34.3 per hour, from a baseline in the mid-50s per hour.

NYSE · As of 11:36 AM ET 11/24/26.

Patients receiving the drug also experienced moderately high weight loss, with trial participants losing as much as 22% of their body weight over the 80-week clinical trial.

Eli Lilly already markets its GLP-1 weight-loss drug, Zepbound, as a treatment for sleep apnea. Yet if Retatrutide is approved for sale and proves itself to be a stronger option among weight loss drugs, the same may potentially occur for this drug candidate. In turn, this could benefit Eli Lilly in the following ways.

Improved weight loss, sleep apnea, and diabetes treatments enable the firm to further deepen its competitive edge against rivals like Novo Nordisk and against drug companies just entering the GLP ring, such as Pfizer.

In turn, the company could continue to experience elevated levels of revenue and earnings growth. While an earnings miss, concerns about its nearly 30x forward multiple, or market changes could send Lilly shares down, a further advance of its key growth catalyst could help it stay one of the best-performing pharmaceutical stocks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 24, 2026 at 10:28AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Chase Coleman's Tiger Global is one of the preeminent technology-focused hedge funds in the world, with many investors who have worked under him eventually starting their own successful funds. In the third quarter, the billionaire tech investor was busy trimming many of his larger stakes. However, one area he was buying was artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductor stocks, increasing his positions in Nvidia (NVDA -8.37%), Cerebras (CBRS -11.36%), and Intel (INTC -9.94%).

Let's look at what Coleman may find attractive in these AI stocks.

At the end of Q2, Nvidia was only Tiger Global's third-largest holding, but three months later, after Coleman bought more shares, Nvidia was its largest holding, representing over 13.5% of its portfolio. While the stock has been on a roller-coaster ride in the past two months, there is still a lot to like about it.

NASDAQ · As of 11:35 AM ET 11/24/26.

Nvidia continues to see incredible growth despite its size, with its revenue more than doubling last quarter and the manufacturer forecasting 75% revenue growth next fiscal year. Despite that, the stock trades at a forward P/E of just 10 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates.

In a recent development, while Nvidia is facing intensifying competition in the data center segment, it still holds distinct advantages. The firm has transformed itself into a complete AI infrastructure player and, as such, is starting to capture a larger share of the revenue pie. With its Grace Hopper architecture, it was getting about $18 billion per gigawatt of capacity, while with Grace Blackwell, it captured around $25 billion per gigawatt. With the addition of more chips to its platforms, such as language processing units (LPUs) for inference, and an expanded software stack, it is now getting $40 billion per gigawatt with Vera Rubin. Meanwhile, Nvidia has locked up vital fab capacity and access to scarce high bandwidth memory (HBM) that will help it maintain its leadership in the data center segment.

Cerebras is one of the most interesting AI chip stocks, in my view, and may have the most upside potential of any. The company's chips are the fastest for inference, but due to their unusually large size and their unique power management and cooling requirements, they are also expensive. This has made its systems more of a niche solution, and the company often rents out capacity on them to clients.

NASDAQ · As of 11:37 AM ET 11/24/26.

However, Cerebras has a major commitment from OpenAI and has secured deals with Amazon, Oracle, and Microsoft. The tech giant has also teamed up with Advanced Micro Devices for a cheaper disaggregated solution that uses Cerebras systems for the ultra-fast decode phase of inference and AMD's GPUs for the pre-fill phase. Analysts at Morgan Stanley have projected that the total addressable market for fast inference will surge from around $4 billion this year to $550 billion by 2030. That's a huge opportunity. Tiger Management added about 1.45 million shares to its position in Q3, increasing its share count by about 48%.

In a recent development, intel is the third chip stock that Coleman bought in Q3. His timing wasn't the best, and investors can now grab the stock at a much lower price than Tiger Global was paying, as the organization issued weak guidance in late October amid a weakening PC market. High memory prices have pushed up computer costs, decreasing demand, and Intel still has considerable ties to the PC market.

Intel's central processing unit (CPU) server opportunity and the potential to turn around its money-losing foundry business are what likely attracted Coleman to the stock. Data center CPU demand is presently through the roof, given the emergence of AI agents, which require far more of them than prior iterations of AI. In servers built for AI model training, the ratio of GPUs to CPUs is 8 to 1, but for those being used to handle inference workloads — the actual use of the models — the ratio dropped to 4 to 1. For agentic AI, which involves less of the heavy parallel processing that GPUs provide, and more computing tasks that must be handled sequentially (which CPUs are built for), the ratio is heading toward 1 to 1.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Intel has spent a boatload of money over the last several years building new fabs in the hopes of competing more effectively with the world’s leading foundry, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. Intel hit a major milestone earlier this month, announcing that it had signed its first external customer deal for its 18A chip fabrication technology. If Intel's foundry operation can become a viable alternative to TSMC for high-end chipmakers, that would be a huge boost to the manufacturer.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 20 November 2026.

This time, Matthias Jaissle wants his fingerprints on the bank notes. But what the head coach wishes for in January, and what Newcastle United are willing and able to give, is likely to be very different. When that happens, it rarely ends well - on the pitch or off it.

The need for reinforcement is clear, even on the back of £270million invested in the summer. Jaissle knows as much and is not afraid to say so. The rookie German has to protect himself as much as he does his club.

Because, as Newcastle prepare for what threatens to be a long and testing winter, Jaissle is revisiting the brochure presented to him in the summer. And that is the 38-year-old's concern and frustration - the prospectus for the season ahead was not of his making.

He arrived three weeks before the start of the campaign and with four of eight signings already through the door. At a cost of £110m, that quartet have started just three Premier League games between them, and each of those by teenager Sean Steur. Baz Toure and Aladji Bamba are virtual spectators, while reserve keeper Ewen Jaouen is injured.

For Jaissle, you suspect, that money was not spent as he would have advised, had he been in situ. Now, in the new year, he wants greater control, as well as a No 10 and No 9. For any Newcastle follower averse to tension, you best watch this transfer window through your fingertips.

Industry observers note that jaissle, sporting director Ross Wilson and chief executive David Hopkinson are the protagonists who will navigate January. At least, that is, if Jaissle makes it into 2027. He deserves that time - not least because of the turbulent and transitional situation he inherited - but the next four fixtures will potentially make or break him and the season.

Head coach Matthias Jaissle is seeking greater control of Newcastle United's transfer strategy.

Aladji Bamba has been a virtual spectator and joined in the summer before Jaissle's arrival.

After the visit of league leaders Arsenal on Saturday, there is a trip to second-placed Brighton, followed by a seismic home double header in the space of five days against Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United and bitter rivals Sunderland.

It is why, despite rumblings behind the scenes in recent days of potential transfer discord, Jaissle was on message - the collective, club message - when I asked him about the profile of player he might want in January.

'It's not the time to talk about the transfer window,' he said. 'We have players capable to deliver higher performances on the pitch. We have massive quality, not only up front, but throughout the whole squad. We believe we can do better and this is what we now want to influence.'.

However, there was a softening when I sympathised with the head coach over him being judged by a window for which he did not have ownership. Did he, then, want more influence this time?

'Now, it's a different story (compared to the summer), if you're already in and also if you have clarified your clear idea, your clear needs, it's going to be easier,' he remarked.

According to recent reports, 'But the transfer market is still a long time ahead, at least it feels like that right now with our fixtures. Our task, especially from my stance, is to focus on the next match and the upcoming challenges.'.

Recent findings suggest that jaissle knows that his case will only be strengthened by a steadying of results, even though, conversely, more defeats would heighten the need for signings. They have lost four from six in all competitions.

Industry observers note that the problem is that the hierarchy are on the record as stating the summer business went pretty much exactly as they wished and believed they had a squad for the entire season. There are also Squad Cost Ratio limitations. It is understood there is headroom for one player, but not the two the manager would prefer and not at a fee approaching the £51m they paid for Matias Fernandez-Pardo on deadline day.

Jaissle wants a new No 9 to compete with the likes of Yoane Wisse who has one league goal.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo (left) has failed to impress so far at Newcastle after his £51m arrival.

The 21-year-old forward is another problem. He is still to score from seven appearances and there is a fear he is not yet strong enough for the Premier League. Interestingly, Jaissle revealed on Thursday his dismay that he was booked during the 1-1 draw at Fulham last time out for screaming at Fernandez-Pardo to stand up.

It has been revealed that that is not to say Jaissle does not believe in the talent of those brought in. He does. But for a coach in his first season in a major European league, he needs players who can impact today, not tomorrow. He needs, and wants, more experience. One of his first recommendations in August was to sign 31-year-old midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Nico Gonzalez eventually arrived in that position, but the 24-year-old looks like a player who has spent two seasons in reserve at Manchester City.

Sources indicate that so, it is easy to see why Jaissle needs and wants more in January. It is also easy to see why he might not get it. There could be trouble ahead, and that is not just the upcoming matches.

How To Make AI-Assisted Evaluation A Reliable Part Of Your Evals

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chhaya Methani is an AI/ML leader driving enterprise innovation with expertise in AI, recommendation systems and evaluation frameworks.
  • ​As enterprises move AI agents into production, AI-assisted evaluation has become the default way to measure quality at scale.
  • In my experience, the challenge is not configuring an LLM judge but establishing what its scores mean and whether stakeholders trust them enough to act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chhaya Methani is an AI/ML leader driving enterprise innovation with expertise in AI, recommendation systems and evaluation frameworks.

​As enterprises move AI agents into production, AI-assisted evaluation has become the default way to measure quality at scale. Its most common form is LLM-as-a-judge, one model scoring another model’s output. Human review is slow and expensive, while a judge model can grade thousands of responses overnight.

In my experience, the challenge is not configuring an LLM judge but establishing what its scores mean and whether stakeholders trust them enough to act. Judges can favor familiar model outputs, reward verbosity or respond differently to answer order. Without accounting for these biases, your evals can give you false confidence instead of a clear signal.

Here, I share four lessons on making the judge work within a scalable eval harness. My previous article explained why enterprise AI needs that harness to catch regressions before production.

In a recent development, many teams start with one large judge that scores every aspect of quality at once. I recommend starting smaller. Pick the simplest version that answers a question you care about, such as whether the agent completed a specific task, and understand what that score captures and what it misses.

Simple metrics are easier to validate and explain. Composite scores can change for many reasons, making it hard to distinguish product improvements from changes in the judge’s assessment.

In my experience, as our agents took on longer tasks, reviewing their trajectories became much harder. Trajectories still matter, but we shifted our focus to two questions: What results did the agent achieve, and did it hit the required milestones along the way?

Checking outcomes sometimes caught an agent reporting a step it never ran, something trajectory review could miss. We could confirm that agents had actually changed the underlying datasets and had used the right authenticated tools to do it. We ended up with a mix of dataset tests and rubrics checked by the judge.

Industry observers note that LLM judges will make mistakes. The goal is to build a flywheel: Product failures show up in evals, judge errors show up in human review and both feed improvements back into the product and the eval. As your understanding grows, add dimensions, finer-grained scales and harder scenarios. ​.

Judges need clear instructions. A common pattern I see is a rubric that asks the model to rate responses from one to five for “helpfulness” or “accuracy,” with no guidance beyond “One is poor and five is excellent.” The judge fills the gaps with its own interpretation, and that interpretation can change from run to run.

Narrow the definition as much as you can. Instead of describing a one as “bad,” describe the specific ways an agent gets it wrong. For an agent answering policy questions, a one could mean it cited the wrong policy or year, a three could mean it found the right policy but missed an exception, and a five could mean the answer was correct and cited its source.

Recent findings suggest that where possible, break broad dimensions into questions you can check: Did the agent call the right tool? Did it use the correct date range? Did it make unsupported claims?

It has been revealed that ideally, each rubric item is a true-or-false check with clear criteria for what counts as true. In my team’s work, this change significantly improved agreement among our human annotators, as measured by Cohen’s kappa, which corrects for agreement by chance. If trained annotators can’t agree on a criterion, a judge model won’t either.

It has been revealed that specific criteria make scores consistent and explainable. When a score drops, you know which behavior caused it.

Industry observers note that before relying on a judge, check how often it agrees with your human annotators. Have annotators label a representative sample, run the judge on the same sample and compare the results. Overall agreement is a starting point, but the real value is in the disagreements.

Industry observers note that annotator expertise matters just as much. With external annotation vendors, subject matter experts are a must-have. A generalist can tell whether a response reads well, but only a domain expert can tell whether a policy exception or a data change is correct. Without that expertise, you risk aligning your judge to labels that are wrong.

According to recent reports, train annotators with a typical data science workflow, including documented guidelines, representative examples and edge cases, and an independently labeled pilot. With domain experts, review disagreements, refine guidelines and recalibrate before scaling. Use expert-reviewed reference examples for ongoing quality checks and version guidelines to keep labels traceable as the task evolves.

Look for the slices where the judge gets it wrong. These errors are rarely random. A judge may be too lenient on responses that sound confident, struggle with domain terminology or miss errors buried in long multistep traces. Enhancement the rubric, add examples or split the criterion and then measure agreement again.

Recheck alignment whenever you change the judge prompt, swap the judge model or launch a new scenario.

According to recent reports, without trust, metrics don’t drive decisions. I’ve seen teams review dashboards weekly yet change nothing. Then stakeholders doubt the scores and fall back on demos and anecdotes.

Before a metric goes live, align product, engineering and business stakeholders on what each value means and what happens in response. For example:.

• Release Gates: What score, or what drop from the baseline, blocks a release?

• Investment Priorities: Which failing slice gets engineering time next cycle?

• Escalation: What regression on high-risk scenarios triggers review before shipping?

Reliability matters here, too. Run the judge several times on the same data to measure its variance, so noise isn’t mistaken for a real change. A metric that can’t distinguish a regression from noise shouldn’t gate a release.

Sources indicate that AI-assisted evaluation scales review, not the work of defining quality. Start with clear instructions and a narrow, trusted metric, then add complexity as alignment and process mature. Evals that evolve with the product drive decisions rather than remain limited to reporting.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • So while Duke Energy does have some defensive characteristics, history suggests you shouldn't expect its stock to escape a market crash unscathed.
  • Unlike companies selling discretionary products, Duke Energy provides essential services that households and businesses continue using during economic downturns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jeff Siegel – Nov 24, 2026 at 10:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Duke Energy ›.

Duke Energy (DUK +1.72%) fell approximately 37% during the COVID-19 market crash in 2020, compared with a roughly 34% decline in the S&P 500. During the 2008 financial crisis, however, Duke held up much better, falling about 39% compared with a 55% decline in the S&P 500.

So while Duke Energy does have some defensive characteristics, history suggests you shouldn't expect its stock to escape a market crash unscathed.

Unlike companies selling discretionary products, Duke Energy provides essential services that households and businesses continue using during economic downturns. More specifically, the company provides electricity to approximately 8.7 million customers across six states and natural gas service to another 1.6 million customers.

According to recent reports, most of its utility operations are regulated, meaning state regulators oversee the rates it charges customers. This generally provides more predictable revenue and earnings than businesses dependent on consumer spending. And the company's latest financial results reinforce that stability.

According to recent reports, Q3 2026 adjusted earnings reached $1.99 per share, up from $1.81 a year earlier. Management also narrowed its full-year adjusted earnings guidance to $6.70 to $6.80 per share, expecting results near the upper end. Looking further ahead, Duke continues targeting annual adjusted earnings growth of 5% to 7% through 2030.

NYSE · As of 11:39 AM ET 11/24/26.

In a recent development, duke Energy's dividend is another reason you may consider holding the stock during a downturn. After all, regular dividend payments can provide income even when share prices decline. Reinvesting those dividends during a sell-off can also allow you to accumulate additional shares at lower prices. That noted, dividends don't prevent capital losses, and future payments aren't guaranteed.

According to recent reports, duke's substantial infrastructure spending requirements also deserve attention. The tech giant is at the moment pursuing a $103 billion capital investment plan to modernize its electricity infrastructure, expand generation capacity, and accommodate growing demand. Those investments support future earnings growth, but they also require significant financing.

Utilities are particularly sensitive to interest rates because they typically carry substantial debt and regularly borrow money to finance infrastructure projects. If a market crash coincides with rising borrowing costs, Duke could face pressure from higher financing expenses.

Higher bond yields can also make utility dividends less attractive relative to safer fixed-income investments. And while Duke's regulated operations provide stability, regulators don't automatically approve every proposed rate increase. Consequently, the organization could experience pressure on earnings and its stock valuation even if electricity demand remains relatively resilient.

Industry observers note that duke Energy wouldn't be my first choice for seeking substantial capital appreciation. Its regulated business generally produces steadier, more predictable growth than many technology or biotechnology companies, but if you're prioritizing income and long-term stability, Duke offers some attractive characteristics.

Its essential services, regulated earnings, and dividend provide a foundation that could help the organization withstand an economic downturn. Still, its performance during previous crashes demonstrates that defensive doesn't mean immune.

Overall, I'd consider Duke Energy a reasonable long-term holding if you're a conservative income investor, but not a substitute for cash or Treasury securities when protecting against a sharp market decline.

Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

📅 28 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5216 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.
  • They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under latest manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect.
  • City created enough space for themselves through clever movement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under latest manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

It has been revealed that however, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He remarked: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Recent findings suggest that maresca stated: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

In a recent development, leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the latest Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

In a recent development, sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

According to recent reports, “I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a upcoming manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ.

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ.

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

Recent findings suggest that the second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

According to recent reports, crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”.

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

According to recent reports, manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

By Rick Munarriz – Nov 24, 2026 at 10:34AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Comcast ›.

Sources indicate that "Some people say, ‘Give the customers what they want.’ But that's not my approach," Steve Jobs once noted. "Our job is to figure out what they're going to want before they do.".

Will Comcast (CMCSA +2.79%) fail to heed Jobs' advice? The entertainment and connectivity giant is trying to give some of its biggest fans what they want. It's been 18 months since Epic Universe at its Universal Orlando resort in Florida became the first major U.S. theme park to open in the last two dozen years.

In a recent development, the park has only been available to those purchasing single- or multi-day admissions, but that's about to change. Late last week, Comcast declared that Epic Universe will be available to add to existing annual passes by early next year.

Comcast is giving its customers what they want. Don't be surprised if things don't go as planned for the country's second-largest theme park operator.

I have been to Epic Universe nine times since it opened in the springtime of last year, buying a single-day ticket every time. My first seven visits took place within April and September of last year. My family took a 14-month break before returning to visit last Monday and Tuesday. Two days later, Comcast would deliver the news that delighted my fellow passholders clamoring for more than just a la carte access to the ambitious theme park.

The gated attraction is gorgeous, unique, and immersive. It's also unforgiving when it's hot or rainy in Florida, something that shouldn't surprise anyone to learn happens often in this peninsular state.

Sources indicate that the biggest problem -- even when it's not scorching hot or a thunderous deluge that shuts down all but four rides -- is capacity. Some of the bar-raising attractions still have pockets of downtime. Even the more basic experiences that don't have reliability issues have low hourly throughputs. The subtraction adds up.

NASDAQ · As of 11:40 AM ET 11/24/26.

Epic Universe lacks the ability to serve as many guests as its nearby sister parks, Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure, or Disney's (DIS +1.30%) four rival tourist magnets. What will happen when annual passes come into the mix starting Jan. 4 of next year?

There are already some rumblings of dissatisfaction, and this is before those floodgates open. Folks generally love Central Florida's hotbed of attractions. The seven other major theme parks within a 20-minute drive of Epic Universe -- Disney World, Universal, and United Parks' SeaWorld Orlando -- have respectable scores on the visitor review site Tripadvisor. They all score between 4.3 and 4.6 out of 5 stars. Epic Universe right now clocks in at a mere 2.5.

There is still a lot to like, if not love, at Epic Universe. I haven't paid for nine single-day admissions because I'm a glutton for punishment. The rich theming is mesmerizing. Outside of Disney World's Epcot, no other domestic park can match its breadth of quality food offerings. The two stage shows are top-notch. There are three exclusive rides that should be on every enthusiast's bucket list. However, if several guests are leaving unhappy now, just imagine what will happen next year, once Universal Orlando passholders -- soon to be called pass members -- pay $120 to $430 more per year than their existing passes for a year of Epic Universe access.

Recent findings suggest that there are three ways that this plays out, and two of them won't be pretty for Comcast stock investors like me. The first scenario is that annual pass members receive less than they expected. Universal will roll out the program in phases, but initially, guests will be limited to two daily reservations. Use one up, then grab another. Disney World has a system like this in place, but availability is plentiful, with tens of thousands of daily slots across its four parks. It should be far more limited and restrictive here. It has to be. Die-hard fans, who thought they were paying for a year-long buffet of thrills, could be in for a rude awakening.

The second grim scenario is that day guests walk away even more dissatisfied. More people mean longer lines under the current capacity constraints. With admissions revenue per capacity dipping into the double digits -- like other parks with a healthy annual pass member base -- the math will prove even more challenging. This may curb the sophomore slump Epic Universe is experiencing in turnstile clicks, but it may come at the cost of burning its highest per-capita revenue segment of visitors on one-day tickets.

The third, and most optimistic, scenario is that the handoff goes smoothly. The ideal fix would have been to boost capacity by fast-tracking high-capacity attractions before Epic Universe even opened. Instead, the first project to break ground was an event center that will open next year. It recently revealed its first newly introduced ride, but that roller coaster is "years" away from opening, according to the announcement.

Industry observers note that there is still hope that Comcast can strike the right balance, satisfying day guests and pass members simultaneously. It won't be easy, but after seeing Comcast shares halved over the past five years, you can't blame the media stock bellwether for taking on an epic challenge to turn around its Epic Universe challenge.

#176725. ​The AI Investment Paradox: Is Sustainable Value Being Built Or Are Technology Costs Just Expanding?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1050 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

​The AI Investment Paradox: Is Sustainable Value Being Built Or Are Technology Costs Just Expanding?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jayasri Ranganathan is VP, Head of Technology Strategy at Trinity Solar | Enterprise AI, Governance & Technology Transformation.
  • An AI solution can reduce processing time, improve productivity and perform exactly as designed yet still fail to deliver a meaningful financial return.
  • Industry observers note that according to Gartner’s October 2026 CIO Survey, only 13% of CIOs reported significant or transformational AI value, while 51% expected AI to increase technology’s total cost of ownership.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jayasri Ranganathan is VP, Head of Technology Strategy at Trinity Solar | Enterprise AI, Governance & Technology Transformation.

An AI solution can reduce processing time, improve productivity and perform exactly as designed yet still fail to deliver a meaningful financial return. This is one of the biggest misunderstandings in enterprise AI investment. Organizations often measure what AI improves within a task without establishing whether that improvement changes the economics of the business.

Industry observers note that according to Gartner’s October 2026 CIO Survey, only 13% of CIOs reported significant or transformational AI value, while 51% expected AI to increase technology’s total cost of ownership. The disconnect is not necessarily a failure of the technology. It is often a failure to connect technical improvements to business outcomes while accounting for the full cost of achieving them.

When evaluating AI investments, I start with a few questions: What business problem are we solving? How will it affect revenue, operating costs, EBITDA, compliance or risk? What will we measure to determine whether the investment delivered?​.

Sources indicate that consider an AI solution that classifies documents and reduces manual processing time. The efficiency improvement may be measurable, but the financial return depends on what happens next. API consumption increases with processing volume. Exceptions still require human intervention. Integrations need maintenance and performance must be monitored.

My experience evaluating AI-enabled processes has reinforced the importance of understanding these production economics. A solution that performs well during initial testing may have a different cost profile at scale.

Industry observers note that there is also the question of what happens to the time saved. Does the organization reduce operating expenses, handle additional volume without increasing headcount or improve service quality?​ If the organization reports hours saved without measuring the operating costs or how that capacity is used, it may be overstating the return.

It has been revealed that AI can improve one part of a workflow while leaving the larger business outcome unchanged. Take a tech giant using AI to identify qualified leads and prioritize sales opportunities. The technology may increase sales activity, but if downstream fulfillment remains constrained or payment cycles remain unchanged, the improvement may not translate into stronger margins or cash flow.​​.

Industry observers note that AI can generate responses quickly, but the organization remains responsible for their accuracy. Where information requires validation or errors carry significant consequences, human oversight may still be necessary. That oversight introduces costs. Removing it can introduce risks.

It has been revealed that the appropriate level of automation depends on data reliability, business impact and the organization’s ability to govern the process. Those considerations should be part of the financial evaluation before deployment, not addressed after the solution is operational. For me, the question is not simply whether AI can complete a task faster. It is whether the entire process performs better after accounting for cost, quality, risk and the business outcome.

These process-level outcomes must ultimately be evaluated against the full cost of deploying, operating and governing the AI solution.

Technology leaders must evaluate AI alongside cybersecurity, infrastructure resilience, ERP modernization and other enterprise priorities. An AI assistant may improve customer service productivity. But if customer information is fragmented across systems, investing in data integration may produce greater immediate value and improve the economics of future AI initiatives.

This is a trade-off I consider when evaluating competing technology investments: Is AI the highest-value use of available resources right now? The calculation must include more than licensing and implementation. Data readiness, integration, API consumption, monitoring, cybersecurity, human validation and ongoing maintenance all affect total cost of ownership.

Industry observers note that information risk also matters. AI systems processing personal or confidential information can create regulatory, contractual and reputational exposure if safeguards are inadequate.

Sources indicate that broader infrastructure pressures add further uncertainty. Gartner has predictied that worldwide data-center electricity consumption would increase 26% in 2026, while a subsequent projection in October warned that more than $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure spending could be exposed to impairment by 2030. Cloud pricing, computing availability and supplier economics all influence the long-term affordability of AI investment.

Sources indicate that these costs and dependencies are connected to the central investment question. An efficiency improvement creates business value only when its benefits justify the resources and risks required to sustain it.

In a recent development, organizations should establish expected AI value before approving an investment. In my experience, these four decisions are particularly important:.

1. Establish The Business Baseline: Understand current processing costs, cycle times, error rates, revenue performance or other relevant measures. Without a baseline, improvements are difficult to quantify.

2. Define The Business Outcome And Owner: Decide whether the investment is intended to reduce expenses, increase capacity, improve revenue, strengthen compliance or reduce risk. Business leaders must be accountable for realizing the expected outcome, not just IT for delivering the technology.

3. Evaluate The Economics At Scale: Model recurring consumption costs, exception handling, human oversight and maintenance. Measure cost per completed transaction, not simply the number of tasks automated.

Industry observers note that 4. Agree On When To Scale, Redesign Or Stop: Establish performance and financial thresholds before implementation. Review outcomes at defined intervals and be prepared to redirect investment if the expected value does not materialize.

According to recent reports, business, finance, technology and risk leaders must work together on these decisions throughout the investment lifecycle, not just at launch. AI innovation requires experimentation, but experimentation should not become an indefinite commitment to spending.

AI will continue to create opportunities for organizations to work differently. But deploying more technology is not the same as creating more enterprise value. A technically successful implementation can still be an unsuccessful investment if operating costs rise faster than the benefits or productivity improvements never translate into business results. The CIO’s responsibility is to make those distinctions visible before they become expensive.

As AI investment grows, the most key leadership question will be whether we can demonstrate how the technology improves the economics of the business, not simply how much work it automates. And when the numbers do not support scaling, are we prepared to make the harder decision to wait?​.

This spending made up about 26% of Take-Two's revenue in fiscal 2017. By fiscal 2026, which ended in March, it was 78%. Part of that growth came from the 2022 purchase of mobile game maker Zynga, which added more revenue to the mix in fiscal 2023. In the most recent quarter, which ended Sept. 30, recurrent spending reached 81% of revenue.

It has been revealed that GTA V debuted in 2013, becoming one of the most played video games in recent years. In fiscal 2023, management said the game had sold more than 180 million units. A year later, that number exceeded 200 million, and CEO Strauss Zelnick noted that GTA V and GTA Online were still growing their audiences more than a decade after their release. On the recent Nov. 9 earnings call, he said GTA V has sold "nearly 235 million units worldwide.".

The money didn't stop at the first purchase. GTA Online players kept buying virtual currency, and in the latest quarter, the GTA series grew both recurrent spending and average monthly GTA+ members by double digits. That's the playbook GTA VI could follow for years to come.

In a recent development, management expects record net bookings, its measure of sales during a period from both digital downloads and physical products, of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion in fiscal 2027. Zelnick has mentioned record bookings will establish a newly introduced baseline for the business and put it on a path of enhanced profitability.

But Take-Two is also trying to convert that higher revenue into higher margins. It delivered $367 million in operating cash flow over the last year, but management's guidance calls for more than $1 billion in fiscal 2027.

According to recent reports, recurring spending helps margins and cash flow by extending the life of games that Take-Two has already paid to create and publish. Management has also executed a cost-cutting program to lift profits over the last few years. CFO Lainie Goldstein said the company aims to enhance its margin profile over time.

Industry observers note that this fiscal year, recurrent spending is expected to be in line with fiscal 2026 levels, at about 65% of net bookings, as the initial wave of GTA VI sales shifts the revenue mix. Once those initial sales fade, the long tail of in-game spending should again make up a larger share of the business, which could lift margins, earnings, and cash flow. As Goldstein put it, GTA VI's launch "is just the beginning.".

Industry observers note that take-Two shares closed at $216.61 on Nov. 18, up about 355% over the past 10 years. But they're down 9% over the past year and 19% below their July 7 high.

At about 6.3 times sales and 31 times analysts' fiscal 2027 earnings estimates, the stock is fairly valued for a video game stock. Analysts expect earnings to grow about 26% a year over the long term. That's solid growth that could justify the stock's valuation.

In a recent development, I believe it's worth buying a starter position in Take-Two stock today. GTA VI is a major catalyst, and the GTA V track record suggests it could keep generating revenue for years.

But you might want to wait for Take-Two's official holiday sales report before taking your position. That way, you avoid any negative surprises that might cause a sell-off in the stock, such as initial sales that don't quite meet the high expectations implied by the stock's premium.
