#176723. Why Data Residency Is Not Resilience

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (822 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Why Data Residency Is Not Resilience

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sharad Kumar is Co-Founder and CEO of FluidCloud, which uses Cloud Cloning to move enterprise workloads across any cloud in seconds.​.
  • A few years ago, our tech giant was acquired, and we had to move our infrastructure from one cloud account to another on the same provider, using the same tools.
  • Our team had spent years building cloud security software and knew the provider’s APIs better than most customers ever will.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sharad Kumar is Co-Founder and CEO of FluidCloud, which uses Cloud Cloning to move enterprise workloads across any cloud in seconds.​.

A few years ago, our tech giant was acquired, and we had to move our infrastructure from one cloud account to another on the same provider, using the same tools.

Our team had spent years building cloud security software and knew the provider’s APIs better than most customers ever will. I assumed the move would take a few weeks. It took nearly a year.

Sources indicate that this project comes to mind every time an executive tells me their tech giant could leave its cloud provider if it had to. I’m the co-founder and CEO of a company that helps enterprises move workloads between clouds, and I often ask, “Have you tried to switch providers?” Almost nobody has.

Recent findings suggest that most sovereign cloud programs focus on which country the data sits in. That’s “residency,” which is the easiest of the three considerations hidden inside the word “sovereignty.”.

The second consideration is operational. Who administers the environment? Where do those decisions get made? Could the estate keep running if an external control plane becomes unavailable?

The third consideration is about independence: Can you keep operating without any single provider? An estate can satisfy residency and operational control, and the answer to that one can still be no.​.

Moving a critical workload to a sovereign provider can leave you less able to recover.

According to recent reports, the confinement to one jurisdiction is deliberate, as it’s exactly what you’re buying. It also removes the mechanism hyperscalers use to survive a regional failure: replication to a site that is geographically and legally distant. Two data centers inside one country don’t give you that. A provider that crossed the border to give it to you would be breaking its own promise.

In a recent development, provider choice is the second problem. If a hyperscaler disappoints you, you have alternatives with comparable capability. If an in-country sovereign provider disappoints you, you have a short list, and each option runs its own partly proprietary stack. Leaving a sovereign cloud is often harder than leaving the hyperscaler you left to get there.

So, a migration presented to a board as reducing dependence on significant tech often only moves concentration risk rather than reducing it. If you document it as a deliberate trade-off and assess the residual risk, that’s a defensible decision. If you present it as a risk reduction, it’s an audit finding waiting to happen.

European rules have turned this from a strategy discussion into an evidence requirement.

The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) ​took effect for EU financial entities in January 2025. Its Article 28(8) requires exit prepares for information and communication technology (ICT) services supporting critical or important functions to be “comprehensive, documented and … sufficiently tested and reviewed periodically.” The key word is tested. A blueprint nobody has run doesn’t clear that bar, however long it is.

The EU Data Act has applied since September 2025 and approaches the same problem from the provider side. It lets customers switch providers with no more than two months’ notice, and switching charges disappear entirely on 12 January 2027. That removes some of the contractual and commercial locks. The technical locks stay exactly where they are. The right to leave and the ability to leave are two different things.

Testing an exit plan doesn’t need a replatforming program. Take one critical workload, rebuild it somewhere else and put traffic through it. Use a sandbox if a live target carries too much risk. A dry run that surfaces the problems while they’re cheap to fix still beats a binder.

In my experience, you’ll likely see four things break during this process, in roughly this order.

Identity breaks first, because each provider has its own way of proving which workload is which and what it can touch.

Networking follows, because topology, routing and private connectivity have to be rebuilt on the target.

Encryption and key custody come next, because where the keys live and who can use them are provider-specific answers.

Recent findings suggest that the fourth problem is the one people resist most. Some services have no equivalent on the other side. Managed AI, advanced analytics and vendor-specific governance tooling often don’t exist on a smaller provider at any price. An honest exit test produces that list. The usual conclusion is a divided estate, with regulated workloads in-jurisdiction and the rest wherever the capability exists. That’s a legitimate answer, even if boards rarely welcome it.

Sources indicate that the list is uncomfortable to read. It’s also the first real information a resilience program has, and it’s cheaper to produce on a random Tuesday than during an incident.

Infrastructure you can move is infrastructure you control.

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026.

Tottenham Hotspur have launched an aggressive campaign to recruit Britain's most talented young footballers from rivals, using expensive private education and lucrative professional contracts to lure them in.

Daily Mail Sport can reveal Spurs are targeting the country's most talented Under 15s through a bespoke package, headed by hefty wages when youngsters turn professional aged 17 and free education at one of the country's finest private schools.

And a glimpse of what the future might look like came against Crystal Palace on October 31.

In a recent development, with Tottenham 2-0 up, Roberto De Zerbi introduced 18-year-old academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett in the 88th minute. The eye-catching cameo proved a memorable Premier League debut, and last week earned him the top flight's Creative Moment of the Month award for a mazy dribble through Palace's defence.

It's further evidence of the talent coming through at Spurs. Williams-Barnett is not a product of the new recruitment drive, but he offers an illustration of what the club hope to achieve by nurturing talented youngsters and giving them opportunities in the first team.

That has not always been Tottenham's strength, having endured a decade of failing to turn potential into established first-team players. Since Harry Kane and Andros Townsend made their league debuts in 2012, only three Spurs academy graduates – Ryan Mason, Harry Winks and Oliver Skipp – have made at least 30 Premier League appearances for the club.

A glimpse of what Tottenham's future might look like came against Crystal Palace on October 31 with Luca Williams-Barnett's thrilling cameo off the bench.

Since Harry Kane and Andros Townsend (left) made their debuts, only Harry Winks, Ryan Mason (right) and Oliver Skipp have made 30 top-flight appearances from Spurs' academy.

In a Daily Mail Sport interview last month, ex-Spurs player and manager Tim Sherwood claimed Tottenham's inability to give youngsters a proper pathway to the first team has failed those in the set-up over the past decade, and that the academy may as well be 'closed up'.

It is a record the club are determined to change. Spurs' renewed strategy has been felt across the Premier League's academy circuit over the past year, with rivals anxious at what lies ahead.

The competition for young players is growing. As well as the traditional Massive Six clubs, Newcastle, Aston Villa and Brighton have also become worthy competitors because of the first-team pathways they offer.

Tottenham pay £21,000-a-year fees to St John's Senior School in Enfield, which boasts top grades and facilities. Its most recent GCSE cohort achieved 65.3 per cent grades 9–7, formerly known as A* and A grades. The school's football pitch has 22 water cannons underneath (the same number as Arsenal's Emirates Stadium) and both primary and secondary drainage systems.

According to recent reports, the programme presented to the parents of prospective stars is the key selling point. Spurs have been given permission by the league to provide a Full-Time Training Module (FTTM) programme which allows students more time away from school. They have their lessons at St John's but on three days a week after lunch, they go to the training ground and focus on football. It is the school's responsibility to organise catch-up lessons so education is not missed out on.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Brighton and Wolves were the first adopters of FTTM, and now Spurs have joined them. Where Tottenham have elevated their strategy is in the number of schoolboys whose fees they cover. Daily Mail Sport understands Spurs have awarded multiple FTTMs to pupils, covering fees in excess of £300,000 annually.

Industry observers note that through this, the club have been able to lure in some of the country's best talents. Isaac Allen, who has captained the England Under 15s, joined Spurs from West Ham in August despite Arsenal's attempts to sign him. The 15-year-old struck four goals in three matches at the Under-15 World Cup last month. Gabriel Rigg, 15, was also recruited from West Ham in September, while Spurs beat Arsenal, Chelsea and Newcastle to the signing of Jake Maloney, 14, from Charlton.

The most promising among the cohort is Ashiah Haughton-Sinclair, who in September trained with Spurs' first team. Last season the 15-year-old became the youngest player to feature for their Under 18s, and netted 70 goals and 20 assists.

Troy Parrott (right) came through the youth set-up but struggled for game time behind Kane. He left for AZ Alkmaar in 2024, and this summer signed for Real Betis.

Marcus Edwards (right) is another Spurs academy product who made the grade elsewhere, scoring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium for Sporting Lisbon in 2022.

Spurs' Hotspur Way base, opened in 2012, is renowned as being one of the finest training complexes in European football, and is regularly used by the England team.

Tottenham's ambitions didn't stop there, as they tried to recruit other players from rivals last summer. The club thought Kyran Thompson was joining from Arsenal, before Newcastle snapped up the talented forward at the last minute. Mishel Nduka, also previously at Arsenal, was approached by Tottenham before he chose a lucrative deal at Manchester City.

Daily Mail Sport understands Spurs pay higher salaries than most Premier League clubs – bar Man City and Chelsea – for academy stars signing professional terms aged 17, which is the earliest age allowed.

This is a significant bargaining chip, as many clubs are rigid in what they will offer players signing their first professional contract.

It has been revealed that there is typically the belief that too much, too young can have a negative impact, but Spurs view it as a necessary ingredient in the modern competition for talent. Nurturing academy graduates into the first team negates the need to spend millions later down the line on established players.

The Tottenham aim is for their first team in the next five years to be reinforced by multiple leading academy graduates, after a decade of producing promising talent – such as Marcus Edwards and Troy Parrott, now at Burnley and Real Betis respectively – without giving them a viable pathway at the club.

And those surplus to requirements could be sold for substantial fees. Luka Vuskovic (£50million to Brighton), Will Lankshear (£20m to Middlesbrough), Ashley Phillips (£20m to Middlesbrough) and Alfie Devine (£6m to Preston North End) are recent examples.

Facilities play a part, too. Spurs' Hotspur Way base, opened in 2012, is renowned as one of the finest training complexes in European football.

The 77-acre state-of-the-art complex in Enfield, which cost £45m to build in 2012 and has since seen significant investment, is home to both the first team and academy, as well as being used regularly by England.

Luka Vuskovic was snapped up before his price tag got too high, and then was sold to Brighton for £50million this summer when he couldn't break into the starting line-up.

Will Lankshear earned Spurs another £20m when he left for Middlesbrough.

With Williams-Barnett already offering a glimpse of what lies ahead, Spurs will hope he is the first of many academy graduates to make the leap.

Recent findings suggest that while four of the 15 grass pitches are reserved exclusively for first-team training, the youngsters benefit from being immersed in the same elite environment as the senior professionals they aspire to emulate. It's an arrangement designed to make the pathway from youth prospect to Premier League footballer feel that little bit closer.

With Williams-Barnett already offering a glimpse of what lies ahead, Spurs will hope he is the first of many academy graduates to make the leap, rather than another reminder of the potential they have previously allowed to slip through their fingers.

For a club that has spent the best part of a decade searching for its next homegrown star, the teenager could yet become the face of a long-overdue academy revival.

Why Auto Shops Are Missing From The Claims Automation Conversation

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nayan Nandan, Co-Founder & CEO of Altis AI, building AI-native insurance claims for auto repair shops.
  • Earlier this year, my co-founder and I spent a couple of months on the ground in auto body shops across the Bay Area.
  • Almost every time, the repair gets done right, but the estimate sent to the insurer doesn’t capture all of it: a pre-repair scan, a calibration, a module initialization after the battery is reconnected.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nayan Nandan, Co-Founder & CEO of Altis AI, building AI-native insurance claims for auto repair shops.

Earlier this year, my co-founder and I spent a couple of months on the ground in auto body shops across the Bay Area. We visited more than 50 shops and spent hundreds of hours sitting next to estimators and owners. We wanted to understand why shops that do good work still lose money on insurance claims.

Almost every time, the repair gets done right, but the estimate sent to the insurer doesn’t capture all of it: a pre-repair scan, a calibration, a module initialization after the battery is reconnected. The technician does the work, and the shop never gets paid for it.

Before my current role, I was an investor at a venture capital firm and a consultant at a major management consulting firm. I’ve read a lot of insurance market maps. Very few look at claims from the side that actually fixes the asset. From what I’ve seen, that gap is getting bigger as insurers automate more of the claims process with AI.

Sources indicate that insurers have had a strong couple of years. BCG, citing S&P Global Market Intelligence and NAIC data, puts the personal auto combined ratio at about 92% in 2025, down from 112% in 2022. Rate increases did a lot of the work, according to Triple-I research.

Meanwhile, the average repair check barely moved. CCC Intelligent Solutions reports the average repair cost was $4,818 in 2025, up just 1.7%, the smallest increase since 2017. The cars also got much harder to fix. ADAS calibrations showed up on 28.3% of repairable estimates in 2025, up from 21.8% the year before.

Industry observers note that the number that says the most comes from CCC’s Q4 2025 data on direct repair claims: More than half of calibrations were added on a supplement, not the first estimate. More often than not, the original estimate misses a procedure the car needs, and it gets caught later, if at all.

It has been revealed that there’s a safety side to this, too. In Seebachan v. John Eagle Collision Center, a Dallas County jury returned a roughly $42 million verdict in 2017. The shop had bonded a replacement roof onto a Honda Fit that Honda’s procedures remarked should be welded. The roof failed in a later crash, and the jury put most of the responsibility on the shop.

According to recent reports, the OEM procedure defines what a safe repair includes. The insurer’s estimate defines what gets paid. The shop carries the liability for whatever falls in between.

That same procedure is also the shop’s best argument. A line item backed by the manufacturer’s documentation is hard for an insurer to deny. Finding the right procedure for a specific make, model, year and trim, and then tying it to the damage on the car, takes longer than most estimators have on every file.

In a recent development, insurers saw this coming and invested early. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment of claims adjusters, appraisers and examiners to decline 5% between 2024 and 2034, partly because software can now assess damage from photos.

Faster claims are good for policyholders, but almost all of this is being built for the payer. On one side of a claim, software checks every estimate against the carrier’s rules. On the other, an estimator with a year or two of experience is often working from memory and a stack of PDFs.

The latest AI models can read across thousands of pages of OEM procedures, and they can now be affordable enough to run on every claim, not just the massive ones.

I am the CEO of a company that builds AI tools for collision shops, but my point goes beyond a specific solution. Whatever tools you use, three things are worth doing:.

Industry observers note that 1. Audit a sample of closed files. Pull 20 recent repairs and check which OEM-required operations never made it onto the estimate. That’s a rough measure of what you’re leaving on the table.

2. Get procedures onto the first estimate. Every calibration caught upfront means one fewer supplement and fewer days of cycle time. Carriers also track cycle time on direct repair program scorecards.

According to recent reports, 3. Keep a human in the loop. An estimate the shop can’t defend line by line just creates a longer fight. Use AI to find what’s missing and attach the source, then let someone who understands claims negotiate it.

Sources indicate that with these steps, the biggest challenge I’ve seen is change management. Claims managers and estimators with two or three decades of experience are understandably skeptical of changing how they work, and that’s usually where adoption stalls. ​.

Auto is a good place to start because OEM documentation gives clear, defensible authority for what a proper repair should include. But the same dynamic runs through all of property and casualty. Roofers, restoration companies and contractors all work on insured physical assets. They all have to get paid by a counterparty that is better resourced and increasingly automated.

I don’t think the answer is an arms race between shop AI and insurer AI. The better outcome is both sides working from the same source of truth: the manufacturer’s procedure, tied to each line on the estimate. ​.

Sources indicate that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a substantial day needed to see but this was reality.

In a recent development, “I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

In a recent development, that leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

In a recent development, isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB.

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

According to recent reports, jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

Recent findings suggest that you can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

In a recent development, it’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW.

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

In a recent development, A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU.

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Industry observers note that liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Industry observers note that out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

In a recent development, following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Recent findings suggest that forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels releases a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Industry observers note that ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm.

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

It has been revealed that huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Recent findings suggest that sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F.

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

It has been revealed that the hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

According to recent reports, we are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7.

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The major story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW.

In a recent development, warm-ups. ✔️ pic.twitter.com/viTAI5FqaQ.

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

According to recent reports, on the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”.

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk.

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd.

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another substantial-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their latest clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

Recent findings suggest that the former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

In a recent development, last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Recent findings suggest that both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Rich Smith – Nov 24, 2026 at 10:59AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Kohl's ›.

It's Tuesday morning, investors, and one of the hottest stocks on the market today is... Kohl's Corporation (KSS +16.96%).

Why? Shares of the department store chain surged 13.4% higher through 10:35 a.m. ET this morning after Kohl's beat analyst forecasts for (checks notes) zero profit, reporting pro forma earnings of $1.76 per share instead. Kohl's also beat on sales, reporting $3.5 billion for Q3 2026 versus forecasts of $3.4 billion.

Sources indicate that the story is not quite as simple as that, of course. The zero-profit quarter that Wall Street analysts were forecasting for Kohl's was based on pro forma, non-GAAP profit. Kohl's crushed that estimate, but it also reported $2.15 per share in earnings calculated under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).

Even with more than half that money coming from a tax benefit, Kohl's quarterly earnings would have been nearly $1 per share.

NYSE · As of 11:31 AM ET 11/24/26.

And judging from Kohl's guidance, investors can expect things to get even better -- for a short while at least. Kohl's grew its same-store sales just 1.2% in Q3, and total sales only 1.3%. It also improved gross and operating profit margins, helping to earn much more on the slight increase in sales.

It has been revealed that how long can that last, though? Management sees sales growth accelerating slightly in Q4, but to no better than 2%. Full-year profits will probably be about $4.40 per share, valuing Kohl's stock at about 5.5 times current-year earnings.

This soundsvery cheap. Still, Kohl's expects to get half its profit this year from "tariff refunds" and "tax benefit," with about 20% of the remainder from selling off real estate. These are all one-time items that will be difficult for Kohl's to replicate in the future. I expect Kohl's stock to look very cheap by the end of 2026 -- but when 2027 arrives, it will look a whole lot more expensive.

Sources indicate that caveat investor. Kohl's looks like a value trap to me.

#176708. Tech Report: Before Automating A Role, Audit What It Does

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (785 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Before Automating A Role, Audit What It Does

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dan Haiem is the founder and CEO of AppMakers USA, helping business leaders design, build and scale apps that deliver real-world impact.
  • Every time someone claims, “We can automate that,” I think of “the doorman fallacy” that marketer Rory Sutherland shared in his book Alchemy.
  • It goes like this: A manager looks at the doorman and sees one job: opening the door.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dan Haiem is the founder and CEO of AppMakers USA, helping business leaders design, build and scale apps that deliver real-world impact.

Every time someone claims, “We can automate that,” I think of “the doorman fallacy” that marketer Rory Sutherland shared in his book Alchemy.

It goes like this: A manager looks at the doorman and sees one job: opening the door. An automatic door does that for less money, so the doorman is let go. Then the hotel slowly learns the other tasks the doorman did: greeting guests, noticing who walked in and finding a taxi when it rained.

In May, AI was cited as the leading cause of U.S. job cuts for the third month in a row, with 38,579 cuts, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas. I’m not here to debate those decisions, but it’s important that someone at least understands what a role actually does before deciding which ones are necessary.

According to recent reports, in evaluating roles, many leaders only look at their most visible task. A technical support answers tickets, a QA finds bugs and a project manager sends updates.

Recent findings suggest that those verbs are often easy to automate, but they also miss the judgment, relationships, small catches and in-betweens. In my experience, a good QA engineer knows which bug a client will actually notice. A good support rep knows which customer is about to leave.​.

Sources indicate that trust me, I’m not against automation. My team automates plenty, but I’ve learned that the most vital question is: Which part of a role is the door, and which part is the doorman?

We’ve automated a few things on my team, and client onboarding is where we learned this lesson the hard way. In our onboarding process, a prospect would fill out the contact form on our site and get an email with an NDA and a link to a questionnaire. Once they submitted it, an automation tool read their answers and decided whether we were a fit.

According to recent reports, it looked efficient but we had a hard time closing clients. It took us a while to connect that to the form. You see, people often fill out a questionnaire just to finish it. I know because I do the same sometimes, especially when I’m busy. You pick whatever gets you to the next screen.

In a recent development, A real project, though, with its half-formed ideas and open questions, rarely fits in a dropdown. Short answers and ticked boxes told us very little about what they actually needed. I now believe that was one of the reasons. We had automated a judgment call, not a door.

Now, we get on a call first and have a real conversation, with follow-up questions about what they’re trying to solve. A form can only ask the questions you thought of in advance. A conversation can follow the answer that surprises you.

According to recent reports, only once we agree it’s a good fit does the NDA, contract and other paperwork run on automation. Based on what I’ve seen, prospects appreciate that conversation more than any form.

Industry observers note that if you’re under pressure to show AI savings, here’s what I’d do before touching a role. Write down everything the role does, including things that go beyond its stated description. Ask the person doing it, because they know what they catch.

Industry observers note that based on those insights, sort each item as mechanical, judgment or relationship. Mechanical work is repeatable and rule-based. Judgment is deciding when the rules don’t fit. Relationship is anywhere the other person cares that you’re human.

Automate the mechanical bucket first, and only that one. In our case, the paperwork that follows a yes was the right thing to automate. Our onboarding form went wrong because we let a tool make a judgment call that looked like a form field.

According to recent reports, if a step needs follow-up questions to get to the truth, it belongs in the judgment bucket. In that case, keep at least one human touchpoint to build that trust. For us, that’s the discovery call.

In my experience, none of this takes long. It’s an afternoon with the person who does the job and a whiteboard.​.

AI is going to automate a lot of doors, and plenty of them deserve it. Before you do, find out who’s standing there and what they actually do all day. Creating savings on the spreadsheet is easy. The value you can’t see is the part you only notice after it’s gone.​​.

Q3 free cash outflow declined approximately 30% from the previous quarter, falling from $1.48 billion to $1.04 billion.

That's roughly $440 million less cash consumed in three months. For a company trying to get its spending under control, that absolutely matters. Every dollar Lucid preserves gives it more breathing room to fund operations and drive a potential turnaround.

But before investors declare the turnaround underway, there's a distinction worth making. Freeing up cash today and building a business that consistently needs less cash aren't quite the same thing.

Sources indicate that free cash flow measures operating cash flow after capital spending. It helps show how much cash Lucid's business consumes, beyond what an earnings headline tells investors. Management credited its operating reset, including aligning production with demand, reducing inventory, and lowering operating expenses, for the sequential improvement.

Sources indicate that lucid Gravity SUV. Image source: Lucid.

In a recent development, inventory management is part of that improvement and, in Lucid's case, needed. Selling vehicles already built while reducing purchases can release money previously tied up in the business. Excess inventory leaves cash parked in vehicles that may eventually require discounts or write-downs – hardly ideal when Lucid needs that money elsewhere.

Rival Rivian Automotive (RIVN -0.85%) is an example of the opposite side of that cycle. It said inventory purchases supporting the R2's launch contributed to Q3 operating cash use. Building up for a launch requires cash; drawing down an existing stockpile can help release it.

It has been revealed that that's why the reason behind cash consumption matters. Spending to support a fresh vehicle launch and freeing cash from excess inventory tell different stories. Lucid's improvement is welcome, but investors still need to see how much spending it can eliminate beyond clearing the excess inventory.

NASDAQ · As of 11:32 AM ET 11/24/26.

Sources indicate that inventory reduction can help in Lucid's trek to improving cash flow, no doubt, but Lucid can't keep shrinking inventory forever. Eventually, it needs enough materials and finished vehicles to support customer demand.

Industry observers note that reducing recurring expenses offers a different benefit. Lucid projected approximately $158 million in annualized savings from its June workforce restructuring, which it substantially completed during the third quarter. Those savings could keep helping after the inventory cleanup runs its course, although spending elsewhere could offset some of the benefit.

Capital spending deserves a closer look, too. It actually increased from approximately $254 million to $287 million sequentially, meaning Lucid's cash-flow improvement didn't come from simply slamming the brakes on investment. Management's broader strategy includes delaying and reducing capital spending, but postponing a bill isn't the same as eliminating it.

Inventory reductions, recurring expense cuts, and capital-spending adjustments all feed into Lucid's cash-flow improvement initiative. The question is whether recurring savings can keep cash consumption down after the inventory cleanup runs its course.

While Lucid's Q3 cash outflow improvement is encouraging, consuming more than $1 billion in a quarter still leaves plenty of work ahead.

Investors will also want to keep an eye on whether operating cash use keeps improving, and whether Lucid can control expenses while preparing its delayed Cosmos vehicle and midsize platform. Launches such as that can be expensive and complicated, and Lucid has a bit of a history with speed bumps in production (even if sometimes primarily a supplier problem).

Sources indicate that investors don't need to dismiss the progress because some benefits won't repeat forever. This was real improvement. Selling down excess inventory and lowering ongoing costs are worthwhile steps. But one better quarter doesn't establish a lasting turnaround. Lucid's cash problem got smaller this quarter. The next few reports need to show it can stay smaller.

  • Nvidia is also under scrutiny for potentially violating U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Foelber – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:02AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

The stock market just had its worst week of 2026 that left many artificial intelligence (AI) stocks in a full-blown crash, rapidly dropping 10% to 20% or more.

As of market close on Nov. 20, Nvidia (NVDA -8.37%) was down 42.1% in just one month and 32.7% since CEO Jensen Huang admitted to marital infidelity. Reports indicate that the Securities and Exchange Commission is conducting a civil investigation into Nvidia for investor disclosures and accounting issues.

Nvidia is also under scrutiny for potentially violating U.S. export controls by allowing restricted AI chips to make their way to China. On Nov. 19, California Attorney General Rob Bonta hit Nvidia with a subpoena based on Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. On Nvidia's Nov. 17 earnings call, management made it clear they did not intend to bring back Huang.

Sources indicate that but before the market opened on Nov. 23, Nvidia published a press release that its Board of Directors had unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as CEO after “a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

But Huang and the manufacturer still face ongoing probes for past actions.

In a recent development, in a stunning reversal, Nvidia gained 31.5% in a single session to close Nov. 23 at $165.05 per share. Even when factoring in that gain, Nvidia is down 31% from its all-time high, while Broadcom (AVGO -3.84%) is 34.9% off its highs.

Here's what investors need to see from Nvidia, and whether Broadcom is a better semiconductor stock to buy now.

Sources indicate that nvidia makes the world's most advanced AI chips and has grown its data center market share by delivering rack-scale supercomputers that integrate graphics processing units (GPUs), central processing units, and networking infrastructure. It is attracting spending from hyperscalers, AI labs, start-ups, and enterprises. Nvidia has only been shipping chips under its most advanced platform (Vera Rubin) since August — giving it a clear runway for near-term growth, with management already forecasting 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, even though Nvidia is still in the middle of its fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

So based on financial results alone, Nvidia looks too cheap to ignore and arguably the best stock to buy in the entire market. There's just one problem.

Sources indicate that nvidia was in free fall because the investment thesis seemed to fall apart in a dramatic, sudden way. Nvidia seemed unbreakable, like accidentally knocking a basketball off a shelf; investors were confident it would bounce back eventually. Only that basketball ended up being a glass trophy rather than court-approved. And investors are left picking up the pieces, wondering what went wrong.

Sources indicate that huang's return as CEO isn't a magic wand that automatically mends the investment thesis. There are still cracks, such as potential repercussions of external and internal investigations. And given how rapidly Huang resigned and the board and management moved on, only to end up bringing back Huang anyway, it's clear that Huang's second stint as CEO is much more fragile than his first. There's still the risk that investigations could provide grounds for removing him down the road. Or that Huang gobbles up even more power against a senior leadership team that seemed so willing to move on without him.

Industry observers note that still, Nvidia is certainly better off with Huang at the helm than without. Without Huang, Nvidia risked deteriorating some of its relationships with customers and suppliers and, even worse, losing some of its top talent.

If Nvidia maintains its innovative edge, improves its governance and organizational structure, and positions the manufacturer to function without Huang, the stock will look like a generational buying opportunity in hindsight.

As tempting as buying the dip on Nvidia may seem, I think a better approach is to scoop up shares of other top growth stocks that have suffered collateral damage from the broader industry sell-off.

Broadcom fell a staggering 12.2% on Friday and only recovered 3% on Monday. It is in an even bigger drawdown than Nvidia.

Broadcom is arguably the most well-rounded semiconductor stock on the market. It designs custom AI accelerators for some of the largest hyperscalers. You may have heard that Alphabet (GOOG -1.48%) (GOOGL -1.59%) is making more of its own custom AI chips for AI training and inference and has begun selling some of these chips to third-party customers. These chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), are designed in partnership with Broadcom.

According to recent reports, alphabet uses TPUs for its Gemini large language model, to power AI features across its platforms, and rents out TPU compute on Google Cloud. TPUs reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs and give Alphabet greater control over its AI stack. And because the latest TPU 8t and 8i chips are custom-built for AI, they have proven to be highly efficient. Which is why Alphabet and Broadcom are now selling compute to hyperscalers, including a deal with Anthropic declared in April for multiple gigawatts of next-generation compute to train and run Claude on TPUs.

As large as Broadcom's business is with Alphabet, Anthropic (ANT -13.23%) and OpenAI could soon surpass Alphabet and Meta Platforms (META -1.56%) as Broadcom's largest customers.

In a recent development, aside from AI chips, Broadcom is a leader in AI networking, general-purpose semiconductor solutions, and infrastructure software. In its latest quarter, which was third quarter fiscal 2026, Broadcom reported $29.6 billion in total revenue, 56.4% of which was AI semiconductor revenue. So AI is by far Broadcom's fastest-growing segment, but there's a lot more to the business outside of AI.

Recent findings suggest that that diversification supports high free cash flows, a stable and growing dividend, and stock buybacks. In the first three quarters of fiscal 2026, Broadcom paid $9.28 billion in dividends and repurchased $8.45 billion of stock, compared with $2.45 billion in the first three quarters of fiscal 2025.

It has also paid a growing dividend for 15 consecutive years. Hock Tan is an exceptional CEO and has led the manufacturer for 20 years. Investors looking for a balanced semiconductor company with strong leadership may want to take a closer look at Broadcom.

It has been revealed that while Broadcom hasn't sold off as much as Nvidia, its valuation has also gotten far more attractive. Broadcom now trades at just 16.2 times forward earnings compared to 17.1 for Nvidia.

It has been revealed that even with Huang back as CEO, Broadcom's investment thesis is far more intact than Nvidia's. And while Broadcom would see an earnings hit from an AI spending slowdown, it has the fundamentals to endure.

Add it all up, and Broadcom stands out as one of the best AI stocks to buy now.

In a recent development, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Industry observers note that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

Industry observers note that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

What drone footage revealed about Mauricio Pochettino's Man United tactics: How he'll set up with and without the ball, a change of role for Bryan Mbeumo and his intriguing use of Joshua Zirkzee

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:10 EST, 20 November 2026.

While thinking over the last few days about his first press conference as Manchester United boss, Mauricio Pochettino would not have expected drones and the fresh Grand Theft Auto video game to be top of the agenda.

Having touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, taking a private jet laid on by United in the immediate aftermath of the United States’ game in Cincinnati against Haiti, it has been a whirlwind 48 hours for Pochettino and his staff.

On Thursday, he took charge of training for the first time against the backdrop of question marks around Bryan Mbeumo’s decision to post late into the night about popular new video game GTA VI.

By the time the day ended, the issue at hand was far more pressing as a drone pilot filmed and uploaded to YouTube a 12-minute video from Pochettino’s first session at Carrington.

How worried Pochettino actually is about the footage – which has since been pulled from YouTube, with a grovelling apology issued – remains to be seen but only this summer did the Argentine concede that ‘we are in an era of spies’.

The footage wasn’t a tactical golden ticket for Liverpool, but what was there to take from it?

A drone pilot filmed and uploaded to YouTube a 12-minute video from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager.

The players get to work, with United's coaching staff seemingly unaware that their every move is being followed from the skies.

Pochettino sides have had a consistent set-up with and without the ball over the years.

The Argentine and his staff have, more often than not, leaned into a back-three in possession, shifting to a back-four without the ball.

In the drone footage we could see the United squad divided into three groups with one XI out on a different training pitch with Pochettino and coach Toni Jimenez.

That group were lined up in what appeared to be that preferred in-possession set-up, with academy defender Reece Munro tucking in from right back to form a back-three alongside Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven, traditional centre backs in a back-four.

Pochettino likes to have at least one full back push on extremely high to provide the width and in this snippet of his first training session, that responsibility landed on the shoulders of teenager Harry Amass, who has struggled for minutes this season, getting a total of just 29 under Michael Carrick.

The United players are put into position by Pochettino at Carrington.

Similarly, Pochettino has often shown a desire to play No 10s – or attacking midfielders – quite narrow. And that is what we saw here, with Amass and Mbeumo providing the width. Mbeumo was on the right of a 4-2-3-1 shape with Matheus Cunha and 17-year-old academy talent Jaume Camacho playing narrower and Joshua Zirkzee up front.

The formation becomes a 3-2-4-1 in possession with the full back pushing on to the wing, creating two No 10s behind the lone striker.

The footage was significant in that it demonstrated Pochettino is implementing his ideas from day one and is wasting no time in trying to embed a style he needs players to get up to speed with swiftly.

But little should be read into the personnel given it was an amalgamation of young players and senior regulars.

We could see academy players Amass, Camacho and Munro among the 10 outfield players, along with Cunha, Heaven, Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Zirkzee.

Of the 10 that were put to task by Pochettino, only four have started more than five league games this season.

It is highly improbable that the personnel used will be anywhere close to the starting XI at Anfield on Sunday.

The footage also revealed games of one-touch rondos going on between the two other groups which were divided between the rest of Pochettino’s coaching team, which includes his son Sebastiano and Miguel D’Agostino, as well as trusted assistant Jesus Perez.

Pochettino greets his fresh players including Bryan Mbeumo, who lined up out wide in the first training session.

United's players start a 'rondo', where one defender stands in the middle and tries to pinch the ball from the players stood around the edge - who are allowed one touch at a time.

One group included Diogo Dalot, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui. The other was academy-led with Bruno Fernandes leading a rondo that featured Shea Lacey, Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Dan Armer, as well as Jaydan Kamason.

But the use of Mbeumo in Pochettino’s work was one of the most interesting aspects, largely because he was back operating in a wider role.

Industry observers note that with injuries hampering Benjamin Sesko, Mbeumo has had to spend a lot of the season deployed through the middle. That could well have to continue given Sesko is not anticipated to return until late January, but Pochettino’s decision to use Zirkzee as the figurehead in his set-up was intriguing.

In a recent development, pochettino’s principles and set-up won’t vary too much; the onus now is on players to adapt. But Pochettino and Jimenez did look to have players in the correct positions. There were no obvious experiments – which makes sense when time is of the essence.

Amass plays off the left, Munro is a centre back, Maguire is comfortable in the middle of any back three, Camacho plays as a No 10 in the academy, both Mainoo and Santos have played together in a double pivot at the base of midfield and Zirkzee is a centre forward.

Pochettino likes a centre forward who can drop in to allow No 10s to run beyond and that suits Zirkzee’s style well, allowing him to be involved as a link man and not isolated with his back to goal.

Mbeumo works better running in behind as a counter-attacking striker, playing on the shoulder of the last defender.

How Pochettino uses Mbeumo over the longer term remains curious because swap out Camacho for Fernandes and Amass for Dorgu and there is a plausible set-up for success, with Mbeumo holding width on the right, Cunha and Fernandes in those central pockets they crave most, and Dorgu holding width off the left.

Lisandro Martinez (left) and Leny Yoro also meet Pochettino and his staff at Carrington.

Pochettino’s track record of working with and improving young players became immediately apparent, with so many given an introduction to his staff and their methods on day one.

While both Jack and Tyler Fletcher, along with Amass, Lacey and Bendito Mantato have made their first-team debuts, it was a golden opportunity in particular for Camacho, the stand-out player in the academy this season following the exit of JJ Gabriel.

United routinely promote multiple academy players each day to bolster numbers in first-team training sessions and it’s a good way for staff to bridge the gap in speed, physicality and intensity between senior and youth football.

Every manager that comes in likes to take on a project and when Ruben Amorim walked through the door it was Godwill Kukonki that caught the eye of staff.

Gabriel became a training mainstay in the months prior to his bombshell request to terminate his contract, and now Camacho, Munro and Armer are working towards first-team debuts instead.

10 stocks we like better than Airbnb ›.

In a recent development, the rise of the gig economy has produced two dominant platforms that changed how people travel and commute. Deciding between Airbnb (ABNB +0.58%) and Uber Technologies (UBER +1.70%) requires looking at their different paths to growth.

Sources indicate that airbnb operates a high-margin marketplace for lodging and experiences, while Uber Technologies focuses on high-frequency mobility and delivery services. Both companies have moved past their early loss-making stages to become profitable enterprises. This comparison examines their business models, financial health, and current valuations to determine which stock is better positioned for investors through 2027.

In a recent development, airbnb operates a massive global marketplace for stays and unique experiences, supporting more than 9 million active listings across 220 countries and regions. The company maintains a specialized Co-Host Network that pairs property owners with support personnel and utilizes Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -1.64%) for its critical cloud infrastructure. This strategy contributes to the growth of consumer discretionary stocks within the global travel market.

During the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, the firm reported that revenue reached about $13.9 billion, representing a growth rate of roughly 16.7% compared to the previous year. Net income for this period was around $3.2 billion, reflecting a consistent demand for travel across major markets like the United States and the United Kingdom. This financial performance highlights the ability of the platform to generate significant profits while expanding into newer geographic territories.

Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, which measures total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio is roughly 1.4x, which compares current assets to current liabilities to show how easily the manufacturer can cover short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was about $4.6 billion, though note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented roughly 34% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

In a recent development, uber Technologies connects riders, drivers, and merchants through a platform that spans mobility, delivery, and freight across more than 15,000 cities. The organization has established major partnerships with retailers like Best Buy (BBY +2.58%) and Tractor Supply Company (TSCO +4.11%) to provide on-demand delivery services to their customers. It also maintains a strategic relationship with Amazon, allowing Prime members to access fee-free orders through its delivery app.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $56.5 billion, which represents a growth rate of approximately 13.9% over the previous period. The firm generated net income of about $3.5 billion during this period, supported by its presence in more than 75 global markets. This growth reflects the continued adoption of its mobility and delivery services by more than 215 million monthly active platform consumers.

In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, measuring the total debt of the company against its shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.1x, which highlights that current assets are sufficient to cover current liabilities as they come due. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached nearly $9.8 billion, providing the company with significant liquidity to fund its operations and expansion looks.

Industry observers note that airbnb faces significant risks from evolving regulatory environments, such as the European Union short-term rentals regulation and local bans in major cities like Fresh York. The organization also manages ongoing tax audits and disputes in several jurisdictions, including Italy and the United States, which could impact financial results. Additionally, competition from traditional hotel chains and search engines like Alphabet Inc. (GOOG -1.48%) remains a constant pressure on its marketplace dominance.

Uber Technologies faces ongoing legal challenges over the classification of its drivers as independent contractors, a situation that could fundamentally alter its business model. The firm competes in a crowded market against well capitalized rivals like DoorDash (DASH +0.35%) and Lyft (LYFT +1.60%) for both drivers and consumers. It also faces operational risks related to safety incidents and the complex technical hurdles of scaling autonomous vehicle technology across its global network.

Based on their current Forward P/E and P/S ratio, Uber Technologies carries a lower valuation relative to its future earnings estimates and sales than Airbnb.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Airbnb reported an excellent third quarter of fiscal 2026, typically its strongest period of the year, beating consensus revenue estimates by some $120 million, reporting $4.87 billion in sales, up 19% from the same period in 2025, driven by a strong increase in booked nights. North America bookings grew at their fastest rate in four years, while growth accelerated in its other major markets, the U.K., France, and Australia.

The business is finding ways to expand its popular travel business, embracing features like buy now, pay later (BNPL) on reservations, a form of short-term lending. Management has also seen great success getting hotels onto its platform, and says 35% of latest Airbnb customers are booking hotels through it. The network advantage of Airbnb's history, over 2 billion guest arrivals since 2008, and the lack of host presence on AI (meaning a competitor using AI has little data to scrape to form a competing product) give it a competitive moat.

For the full year, Wall Street expects sales of $14.4 billion with net income of $3.3 billion.

Industry observers note that uber revolutionized the taxi industry when it rolled out its ride-sharing network, allowing anyone with a car to earn a side gig. Both the industry and the manufacturer have come a long way.

Uber Technologies is by far the largest player in the developing ride-share market by revenue. Wall Street expects Uber's sales to increase by $6 billion from last year to $58 billion this year, accompanied by net income of $6.4 billion. But as a sign of the expenses Uber faces in expanding its business model, that would be roughly $3.6 billion less income than in 2025. In the long run, its global ride-sharing, delivery, and autonomous solutions business will be strong, according to analysts.

So which is the better buy for 2027? Uber trades at just about the average S&P 500 stock in terms of forward P/E, and its P/S ratio is also quite reasonable. That doesn't mean Airbnb is bad, although its premium valuation to its main competitor, Booking Holdings (BKNG +1.91%), causes concern over how Airbnb holds onto its valuation in the long term. That gives the nod to Uber.

#176689. When AI Finds Data It Shouldn’t: Why Relevance Isn't Permission

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (971 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

When AI Finds Data It Shouldn’t: Why Relevance Isn't Permission

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vibhor Kumar is a technology executive and author focused on enterprise data and AI platforms, modern architecture, and technology strategy.
  • ​In one enterprise search project I advised on at a large financial services organization, data from a governed operational system was copied into a separate search layer to improve retrieval speed.
  • Sources indicate that we discovered this when an analyst searched for information and received a client record that the original application would not have allowed that person to see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vibhor Kumar is a technology executive and author focused on enterprise data and AI platforms, modern architecture, and technology strategy.

​In one enterprise search project I advised on at a large financial services organization, data from a governed operational system was copied into a separate search layer to improve retrieval speed. The source system had established access rules. The search copy did not carry them all forward.

Sources indicate that we discovered this when an analyst searched for information and received a client record that the original application would not have allowed that person to see. The search system had not been compromised. It was doing exactly what it had been built to do: finding information in the data available to it.

Sources indicate that even though the information was visible only internally, a user being able to retrieve a client record they were not entitled to see was a serious access-control matter. In a financial services environment, that could become an audit, privacy or compliance problem. What concerned me most was that the system looked healthy technically. There was no failed authentication or obvious security event to alert us. The weakness was in the difference between the controls on the original data and the controls on the copy.

We had moved the data without fully moving the authorization that belonged with it. I have thought about that incident again as enterprises connect more of their data to AI systems, and it shaped three practices I now recommend.

A lot of the discussion about AI data risk starts with the model: whether it could memorize sensitive information, expose something through a prompt or be tricked into returning data someone should not see. Those are valid concerns. But there is another problem that happens earlier. The AI may not need to get around a security control at all. We may already have put the data somewhere it can reach.

Sources indicate that data gets copied into vector stores, search indexes, analytical systems and training datasets, usually for understandable reasons. The source database may have years of work behind its access model: roles, tenant boundaries, retention policies, audit history and application-specific authorization. But the new retrieval layer may reproduce only part of that logic. Authentication does not fix that problem. The system still has to determine whether that user is allowed to retrieve this particular information, in this context, at this time.

The immediate fix in that project was to stop relying on the search copy as if it carried the same authorization model as the source system. The team tightened the retrieval path so that access was checked against the user’s actual permissions before a record became eligible to appear in search results. That experience is one reason I now use the phrase “filter first, search second.” Relevance should be evaluated only within the set of information the user is entitled to retrieve.

According to recent reports, semantic search is very good at answering, “What information is most related to this request?” It should not be responsible for answering, “Is this user allowed to receive it?” Before records become eligible for retrieval, the system needs deterministic controls around tenant, role, geography, entitlement or data sensitivity. If the system retrieves broadly and tries to apply authorization afterward, sensitive information may already have crossed the boundary you were trying to protect.

The more vital change was architectural. We stopped treating security on the source system as sufficient protection for downstream copies. Any latest search or analytical layer had to account explicitly for how source permissions would be preserved, synchronized or enforced at retrieval time.

In a recent development, that does not mean enterprises should stop copying data. Sometimes, a separate index is the right way to meet latency requirements, and analytical replicas can isolate expensive workloads from transactional systems. The distinction I care about is whether the duplication is intentional. When a team can explain why the copy exists, who owns it, who can reach it, how permissions stay aligned with the source and when the copy should disappear, the trade-off is reasonable. Problems start when the copy survives longer than the thinking that created it. At that point, it becomes architectural debt.

Deletion makes the problem tangible. If a record must be deleted, restricted or no longer made available, changing the source is not enough if the same information continues to exist in a search index, vector store, cache, analytical copy or AI dataset. Organizations need to know not only where the authoritative record lives but also where derived representations of that record exist and whether changes in permission, retention or deletion propagate to them. That is a privacy and compliance obligation as much as an architectural one.

In a recent development, A simple test: When a customer, employee or document loses access in the source system, can the organization show that the same information is no longer retrievable from every derived copy? If that answer is unclear, the access model is probably unclear, too.

If a CIO asked me where to begin, I would not start with a large governance program. I would first map where sensitive data has been copied for AI, search and analytics, and then compare those copies with the systems they came from. For each one, I would want to know who owns it, how access is enforced, how permissions change, how deletion works and whether anyone can prove that those controls are still aligned with the source.

AI is making enterprise information much easier to find. But finding the right information is only half the job. The other half is ensuring that it reaches someone who was actually allowed to receive it.​.

In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?
