Delaying Retirement By 1 Year? Here's What It Might Do for Your Finances

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when you set a retirement date, it's natural to want to stick to it.
  • Industry observers note that but if you're not feeling all that confident in your retirement finances, it could pay to be flexible as your planned workforce exit date approaches.
  • The amount of money Social Security pays you each month in retirement is based on your personal wage history coupled with your filing age.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Maurie Backman – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:18AM EST.

Sources indicate that when you set a retirement date, it's natural to want to stick to it. After all, the idea of stopping work and reclaiming your free time can be appealing.

Industry observers note that but if you're not feeling all that confident in your retirement finances, it could pay to be flexible as your planned workforce exit date approaches. In fact, delaying retirement by just a year could do you a world of good. Here are two potential benefits.

The amount of money Social Security pays you each month in retirement is based on your personal wage history coupled with your filing age. If you wait for full retirement age to claim benefits, which is 67 for anyone born in 1960 or later, you'll get your monthly Social Security in full. But waiting could yield greater benefits.

Each year you delay your claim past full retirement age up to age 70 boosts your monthly benefits by 8% -- for life. So if your planned retirement date is 67 but you work one more year and claim Social Security 12 months later, you could score a nice boost to your monthly checks.

According to recent reports, and remember, boosted benefits also mean larger cost-of-living adjustments. You may have an easier time keeping up with inflation in retirement if your annual increases are more generous thanks to having larger benefits coming your way.

Working one extra year may afford you the opportunity to modestly boost your retirement savings. But even a modest last-minute contribution to your IRA or 401(k) could give you more options or peace of mind.

According to recent reports, let's say you work an additional year and contribute an extra $1,000 a month to your 401(k) during that time. Will another $12,000 make or break your retirement? Maybe not.

But could an extra $12,000 take some pressure off your first year of retirement? Probably. That sum could easily pay for a vacation, some surprise home repairs, or other costs you may not have anticipated.

In a recent development, this, of course, is just one example, and the amount of extra money you can save by working another year depends on your personal situation. The key is to not discount the benefit of a last-minute contribution.

#176682. ​How Much Autonomy Is Too Much For An AI Agent?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1034 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

​How Much Autonomy Is Too Much For An AI Agent?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alexey Spas is the founder and CEO of Instinctools, a software engineering tech giant focused on AI-powered digital solutions.
  • ​What happens when an AI agent you trust breaks its limits of autonomy and won’t take no for an answer?​​.
  • According to recent reports, neither the Australian nor the Canadian government was prepared for this kind of trespassing, yet it happened to their websites.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexey Spas is the founder and CEO of Instinctools, a software engineering tech giant focused on AI-powered digital solutions.

​What happens when an AI agent you trust breaks its limits of autonomy and won’t take no for an answer?​​.

According to recent reports, neither the Australian nor the Canadian government was prepared for this kind of trespassing, yet it happened to their websites. An OpenAI model gained unauthorized access to Australia’s Medicare Statistics Reporting Service while researching public medical spending, while an unidentified AI agent attempted to hack Canada’s Library and Archives website. Neither incident resulted in a confirmed compromise of individual records or government systems, but both involved AI agents taking actions beyond their intended research tasks. The activity occurred in May and June 2026 but wasn’t publicly disclosed until September, when OpenAI and the research lab Transluce independently reported their findings.​​​.

What this signals to me is that AI agents are forcing both public and private sectors to raise the drawbridge against a threat they didn’t even know was coming. For companies deploying agents at scale, the governance challenge extends beyond choosing a theoretical level of autonomy to ensuring that abnormal behavior can be detected, contained, reconstructed and assigned to a responsible owner.​.

MIT recognizes five levels of AI agent autonomy. Starting from level 3, as the human gradually steps back to give the agent more room to act, a handoff problem arises. The system needs to recognize where its authority ends and when escalation to a human is required. The harder failure mode appears when an agent continues pursuing a legitimate goal after crossing that boundary, despite signals telling it to stop.​.

It has been revealed that this suggests a useful operating principle: the autonomy granted to AI agents can’t safely outpace the maturity of the firm’s incident response and AI governance policies. Policies on paper are not enough; they need to be enacted. That maturity rests on four capabilities:.

1. Detection: Identifying unusual actions as they happen.

2. Investigation: Tracing back the agent’s actions.

In a recent development, 3. Response: Stopping agent activity and rolling back or mitigating the consequences.

Sources indicate that 4. Accountability: Establishing clear responsibility when an agent’s actions affect a person or a tech giant.

A weakness in any one of those capabilities raises the cost of failure: unusual behavior may go unnoticed, incidents may be harder to reconstruct, containment may come too late or responsibility may remain unclear when an agent’s actions affect people or business operations.

Not every scenario can be rehearsed in advance. So the decision to give an agent any degree of autonomy depends on answering a few questions first:​.

Every consequential output should have a way to be checked—a second system, a source link or a human-created reference—before the agent is allowed to act on it.​.

Industry observers note that the Medicare case above illustrates what can happen when an agent treats a block as something to overcome rather than a boundary to respect. A block should stop an agent in its tracks and trigger escalation to a human. It shouldn’t become an obstacle to work around.​.

Impact should be classified by severity and blast radius. An agent accessing a public webpage poses a different level of risk than one accessing an internal server or sensitive business systems. The more sensitive the data and consequential the actions an agent can access, the tighter its permissions, oversight and safeguards should be.​.

According to recent reports, when several vendors are involved, incident ownership can’t fall through the cracks. From where I stand, someone on the customer side needs to be ultimately accountable, even if detection, investigation or remediation depends on external providers. That means defining from the get-go who detects an incident, who notifies whom and who can switch the agent off.

It has been revealed that the autonomy ladder can only be climbed when the evidence is there. Autonomy should be earned, with each traceable and reviewable log supporting more trust in the agent. The ladder also runs downward. When the environment, model, tools or performance indicators change, the autonomy limits narrow again until the evidence rebuilds.​.

Anthropic found an interesting pattern: upcoming Claude Code owners enable auto-approve about 20% of the time. Past 750 sessions, this rate rises to 40%. Yet experienced users also interrupted their agents more often. Anthropic reinforces that effective oversight is not about approving each action but being able to intervene when necessary.​.

Sources indicate that enterprise deployments can follow the same principle: greater trust should lead to more selective oversight, not less accountability. Rather than relying on subjective confidence in an agent, organizations can use operational metrics to determine whether its autonomy is justified and where additional controls may be needed. NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework Playbook similarly emphasizes incident tracking, response planning and human oversight. Some useful indicators include:​.

• How often humans intervene or override an agent​.

• The frequency of rejected or blocked actions​.

• How often actions require rollback or remediation​.

• Policy violations and near misses​.

• Actions that fall outside expected behavioral patterns​.

• Incidents categorized by action type and severity​.

For a professional services group’s AI operational platform developed at Instinctools, the autonomy was phased in: the low-risk employee assistant agent was deployed before higher-risk quoting and advisory agents. The email triage agent only reached all the business units after its accuracy was raised from 74% to 87%, past the client’s 85% target.

Following MIT’s definition of five autonomy levels mentioned above, I keep returning to this distinction between agents’ autonomy and humans’ authority. Freedom to act within defined boundaries belongs to agents. But authority stays with humans who answer for what agents do and decide if and when their scope is ready to grow.​.

The test is simple: deploy only those agents that stop when told no and only when you have a framework in place to watch and contain them, investigate what happened and take responsibility if needed. If an agent can reason its way around a limit, it’s not a limit.​​.

Industry observers note that while the analyst acknowledged the stock's recent decline, Ackerman remains concerned that hyperscalers orders are getting ahead of themselves. NASDAQ · As of 11:35 AM ET 11/24/26.

"We think DRAM and NAND supply-demand can approach parity starting in mid-2027 and result in ASP [average selling price] declines, earlier than our prior view of mid-2028," Ackerman remarked.

This echoes ongoing investor concerns about the durability of AI demand and historical cyclicality. These concerns have driven Micron down roughly 48% from its recent peak (as of this writing), and the stock now sells for just over 8 times earnings. If you believe, as I do, that AI adoption will continue for years -- if not decades -- Micron stock is certainly worth a look.

  • A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.
  • Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on August 15 last year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:49 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 20 November 2026.

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on August 15 last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, said: 'Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him.

'In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.' District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident but later signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mr Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

The court had heard Mr Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game.

Mark Mogan (right) has been found not guilty of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo (left) after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

He was alleged to have said: 'Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black b*****d.'.

Opening the case last month, Mr Jones said: 'That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

'Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn't believe what the male had stated.' Mr Mogan then shouted "I'm talking to you, you ****", the court heard.

Witnesses also mentioned they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mr Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mr Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to 'hurry up'.

Mr Mogan, of Templehill Close in Dovecot, Liverpool, declined to comment as he left court.

Semenyo, who scored a brace in the game, had brought the incident to the attention of match referee Anthony Taylor and the match was briefly halted while both managers and captains were spoken to.

At half time an announcement was made to the crowd asking for no racist abuse and pictures on social media revealed a man in a wheelchair being escorted along the touchline and out of the ground.

Mogan, pictured with Liverpool legend Robbie Fowler, would have been banned for life if he'd have been found guilty.

Merseyside Police later revealed the man had been arrested and then was bailed for three months pending further investigations.

Pictures on social media showed Mogan playing wheelchair basketball for a team called the Greenbank Meteors while other images show him posing with Liverpool legends Robbie Fowler and Emile Heskey.

After he was charged, Liverpool confirmed he would be banned for life if found guilty but Judge Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty on Friday morning.

  • St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.
  • McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute intends for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.

McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute intends for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.

Mulholland was hoping to ensure teams featured Scotland Under-21 eligible players for an average of 60 minutes per league game and had two on the pitch for each cup tie.

McLeish said: 'That’s damning that he’s having to change his prepares to pander to clubs who aren’t really on board with it and don’t really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

'I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They’re in jobs, they’re all fighting for their clubs.

'But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

St Mirren boss Craig McLeish believes self-interest at clubs is hampering Scottish football.

'It’s the way governance is set up and we’ve killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they’ve got self-interest, and there’s a lot of self-interest at the top end.

'I just don’t see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don’t ever see that happening. It’s really sad.'.

Although McLeish backs quotas, he fears that would not address the root cause of Scottish football’s problems.

'We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base,' noted the 36-year-old, who worked in St Mirren’s youth academy before his current role.

'We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And until you fix that, you can’t fix the top end of it.

According to recent reports, 'It’s crazy some of the stuff that’s going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There’s just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

'In this country, football’s everyone’s sport and everyone gets access to it but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you’re there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

'We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they’re not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

'And you’re just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

In a recent development, 'Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don’t get that right, you’re dead. You can’t do anything after that point, and we don’t do it well enough. And you’re just chasing yourself and we’ll never catch up.'.

The SFA has been contacted for comment.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this year, OpenAI received a $30 billion investment from Nvidia (NVDA -8.34%).
  • OpenAI's frontier artificial intelligence (AI) model ChatGPT and other technologies rely on Nvidia's advanced graphics processing units (GPUs) as the foundational hardware that enables the incredible things they do.
  • With recent shake-ups and uncertainties in the AI space in mind, here's what the big investment deal means for Nvidia shareholders and prospective OpenAI investors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keith Noonan – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:33AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Earlier this year, OpenAI received a $30 billion investment from Nvidia (NVDA -8.34%). While OpenAI has yet to go public, it stands as one of Nvidia's largest investment positions -- and the two companies have an crucial relationship.

OpenAI's frontier artificial intelligence (AI) model ChatGPT and other technologies rely on Nvidia's advanced graphics processing units (GPUs) as the foundational hardware that enables the incredible things they do. On the other hand, CEO Sam Altman's company is one of Nvidia's most important partners, accounting for both direct GPU purchases and compute contracts with third parties that have built data centers around Nvidia's GPUs.

With recent shake-ups and uncertainties in the AI space in mind, here's what the big investment deal means for Nvidia shareholders and prospective OpenAI investors.

Sources indicate that nvidia has taken to investing directly in some leading players in the AI industry in recent years. In some cases, the investments translate into meaningful sales and infrastructure boosts for the processing leader. In other words, Nvidia invests a large amount in a manufacturer -- and that company can then use that capital to purchase Nvidia's hardware.

While this circular financing has attracted criticism from high-profile investors, including Michael Burry and other analysts, it has also helped facilitate growth in the AI industry. On the other hand, it looks like Nvidia will be pulling back, at least somewhat, in providing easy access to capital for its partners in the AI space.

Industry observers note that even before the resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang, the organization was reportedly planning to shift its approach to funding companies that would be major purchasers of its chips. Following Huang's departure, reports suggest that the AI hardware leader will be far more selective in providing investment capital.

NASDAQ · As of 11:31 AM ET 11/24/26.

On balance, Nvidia's $30 billion investment in OpenAI has probably been a good thing for both companies and their shareholders thus far. With Nvidia being the leading provider of AI processing hardware and OpenAI being a leading provider of advanced artificial intelligence software, the two companies naturally have a somewhat symbiotic relationship.

Nvidia's investment helped fund OpenAI's technological advancement and market expansion, and much of that capital went directly toward purchasing Nvidia's high-end GPUs along with related hardware and services.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

On the other hand, these kinds of investment and purchasing relationships look poised to continue attracting scrutiny. For Nvidia, this could mean further downward pressure on its share price and earnings multiple in the near term as investors assess the implications of new investigations and shifts in regulatory dynamics.

For OpenAI, recent controversies surrounding Nvidia and circular AI financing could cause the firm to postpone its initial public offering until the outlook on these fronts becomes clearer.

DoorDash vs. Etsy: Which Consumer Favorite Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 11:39AM EST.
  • In a recent development, should everyday investors prioritize the rapid growth of DoorDash (DASH +0.35%) or the specialized marketplace niche of Etsy (ETSY -0.62%)?
  • According to recent reports, doorDash dominates local logistics by connecting consumers with restaurants and retailers through a vast delivery network.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 11:39AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than DoorDash ›.

In a recent development, should everyday investors prioritize the rapid growth of DoorDash (DASH +0.35%) or the specialized marketplace niche of Etsy (ETSY -0.62%)? Both companies serve distinct corners of the digital economy as they eye 2027.

According to recent reports, doorDash dominates local logistics by connecting consumers with restaurants and retailers through a vast delivery network. Etsy operates a global creative marketplace focusing on handmade and vintage items. While both rely on a two-sided platform model, their growth trajectories and valuation profiles differ significantly for those looking at the next few years.

It has been revealed that doorDash operates a local commerce platform connecting merchants, consumers, and Dashers, who are independent contractors providing delivery services. The company facilitates on-demand delivery for restaurants, grocers, and other retail businesses through its two-sided platform. In its latest annual report, the company noted that it operates in more than 40 countries and ended the year with more than 56 million monthly active people.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $17.1 billion, representing revenue growth of approximately 35% compared to the prior 12 months. During this period, the firm generated net income of around $1.1 billion. This shift to profitability highlights the increasing scale of its marketplace and the growth of membership programs like DashPass.

According to recent reports, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company's debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.3x, calculated by dividing total debt by shareholders' equity. Its current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, was roughly 1.4x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached about $2.2 billion, though stock-based compensation represented roughly 43% of operating cash flow. This compensation level inflates reported cash generation because it is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Etsy runs a global two-sided marketplace for creative entrepreneurs, connecting millions of active buyers and sellers interested in unique or handmade goods. According to its latest annual report, the marketplace serves roughly 86.5 million active buyers and 5.6 million active sellers, many of whom are home-based businesses. This specialized focus helps distinguish the tech giant from broader competition among retail stocks.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue was around $2.9 billion, a figure representing revenue growth of approximately 2.1% over the prior 12 months. The company reported net income of about $987.5 million for the period, resulting in a net margin of roughly 34%. This high level of net profitability reflects the lean nature of its marketplace business model.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Etsy reported a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly -2.8x, which means total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The organization maintains a current ratio of approximately 1.4x, indicating it has sufficient liquid assets to cover short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was about $678 million, while stock-based compensation represented roughly 35% of operating cash flow. This non-cash add-back inflates reported cash generation on the cash flow statement.

DoorDash faces intense competition from local on-demand delivery companies and large-scale retailers. The company is also subject to regulatory and operational risks regarding the classification of its Dashers as independent contractors. Furthermore, the business manages risks involving cybersecurity threats and the financial pressure of maintaining rapid international expansion while relying on third-party payment processors.

Etsy competes with a wide variety of online and offline retail venues, including major platforms like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -1.39%) and eBay Inc. (EBAY -2.51%). The organization's growth depends on its ability to attract and retain both buyers and sellers while managing dependencies on infrastructure providers like Google Cloud from Alphabet Inc. (GOOG -1.58%). Legal risks concerning intellectual property and the complexities of international tax regimes also remain key factors, alongside the pending divestiture of Depop.

Etsy appears to be the more conservatively valued option based on its Forward P/E, while DoorDash commands a higher P/S ratio, measuring market capitalization relative to sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

One of the advantages of Etsy is that individual sellers on the platform are passionate about what they sell and are known for their attention to detail and high customer service. A company with passionate users often has passionate shareholders, too. Metrics such as active buyers and growth in gross merchandise sales per active buyer are improving as the company benefits from personalization and AI initiatives. Etsy's capital-light model means it doesn't need to allocate significant capital to manufacturing facilities or inventory.

In a recent development, still, top-line growth isn't very strong. The company is expected to see a slight $12 million rise in revenue this fiscal year to $2.895 billion. Yet that will come with a more than 550% jump in net income to $1.059 billion, a level Wall Street analysts see as sustainable in the year ahead.

Recent findings suggest that originally a prepared-food delivery service, DoorDash has been finding success by expanding into latest business verticals, such as delivering electronics, apparel, and groceries. Groceries, in particular, are expected to grow twice as fast as meal delivery for the company in the coming years. International expansion, wth the acquisition of the U.K. based Deliveroo, is helping the company expand as well. Advances in efficiency and speed, and improvements that help customers build order carts in the app, are improving sales, too.

For the current fiscal year, 2026, revenue is expected to rise 30% to $17.8 billion, with net income improving about 20% to $1.13 billion.

According to recent reports, so, which is the better buy? Top-line growth makes DoorDash tempting, but the remarkable profit margin of Etsy, coupled with its low forward P/E ratio, is too good to ignore.

By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:39AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than iShares Silver Trust ›.

It was this time last year that silver was on the rise and beginning to take off, eventually hitting a peak of more than $121 per ounce in January 2026. What's happened since then, however, has been a rapid reversal.

In a recent development, today, silver trades at around $40. Along with its free fall, the iShares Silver Trust (SLV -5.05%) , which tracks the price of silver, has also tanked, losing more than 40% of its value this year, and it's down more than 65% from its 52-week high of $109.83.

Given the massive sell-off and reduced valuation, could this silver-focused fund be a good investment right now?

Sources indicate that the substantial question for investors considering this fund is likely what will happen to the price of silver. Will it soar again, or is it destined to go even lower? If it takes off in value again, the iShares Silver Trust will quickly become a hot buy.

The problem is, there's no guarantee that will happen. What took place late last year was unexpected, not unlike what has happened to speculative investments such as meme stocks in the past. Silver caught the attention of retail investors and reached levels it's never reached before. There's unfortunately no reason to expect that might happen again, simply because it is a largely speculative asset.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, as interest rates have increased, there's even been more of a reason to move away from precious metals and into income-generating investments, especially as yields are higher. Thus, it's hard to make a bull case for silver these days.

NYSEMKT · As of 11:34 AM ET 11/24/26.

The main appeal of the iShares Silver Trust today is that it can help diversify a portfolio by giving investors access to investments outside of the broader markets. But beyond that, I don't see a reason as to why silver might suddenly soar once again or why to invest in the fund. A resurgence may not happen until there's reason to believe that interest rates might be coming down again, which doesn't appear likely anytime soon.

Sources indicate that since the performance of the iShares Silver Trust depends heavily on the price of silver, investors should treat it as a speculative, potentially highly volatile investment. While it is down major from its high, there's no guarantee that it'll get back to those levels anytime soon.

CrowdStrike (CRWD +0.82%) declared a definitive agreement to acquire Zscaler for approximately $43.9 billion, a strategic transaction that incorporates network security into the Falcon platform to establish a unified control plane. The manufacturer reported record net new annual recurring revenue and accelerated growth across its primary financial metrics, driven by high demand for AI-driven security modernization. Management stated that the combination of the two cloud-native leaders will cover devices, workloads, identities, data, and the network on a single platform. The quarter was characterized by significant adoption of the Falcon Flex commercial model and the rapid growth of Falcon Guardian, which secures autonomous AI agents. The combined entity is expected to begin with more than $10 billion in ending annual recurring revenue once the transaction closes in the second half of fiscal year 2028.

Industry observers note that these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight fresh signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

It has been revealed that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Industry observers note that roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

It has been revealed that for Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi noted he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH.

It has been revealed that newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

In a recent development, “After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”.

Industry observers note that to be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the newly introduced signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

In a recent development, of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

Industry observers note that there are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

Industry observers note that at least the challenges facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. According to recent reports, “At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. “We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

Recent findings suggest that the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

It has been revealed that tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are at the moment in the ascendency.

Industry observers note that tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

It has been revealed that tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Industry observers note that marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very latest-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Recent findings suggest that tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

In a recent development, newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

In a recent development, we are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Recent findings suggest that captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

With just under ten minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two line-ups this evening.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Roberto De Zerbi has explained Sávio's absence from our matchday squad ℹ️📲 https://t.co/ACZscgieFg pic.twitter.com/ddGz2NveX3.

“It was bad news yesterday before training in the afternoon because he suffered muscle fatigue and the medical staff obviously didn’t want to take a risk and I agree with them - it’s not the right moment, especially because he didn’t work in the last 10 days, for him 20 minutes against Charlton, maybe it was tough to rest for the days after but for the next game I think there are no problems.”.

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm.

"If I'm a Tottenham fan, this is the most excited I've been in MANY YEARS"Jamie Redknapp thinks that Spurs have built a strong squad that can compete in the Premier League 👀 pic.twitter.com/55Dwm7BaoE.

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

HWTL 💪 pic.twitter.com/qR2wOVBZSU.

Crystal Palace 1 Manchester City 4.

Liverpool 2 Nottingham Forest 2.

Tottenham Hotspur vs Newcastle United.

Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Nico will make his NUFC debut today 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ilEM8w3Dwd.

Roberto De Zerbi has remarked that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”.

Tottenham had been hoping to see Savinho following his glittering cameo which yielded a goal and an assist against Charlton on Wednesday, but they will have to wait for his Premier League debut.

Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

It has been revealed that nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB.

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

It has been revealed that marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

According to recent reports, good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his upcoming surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

According to recent reports, despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in upcoming boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Industry observers note that newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

10 stocks we like better than Lockheed Martin ›.

Over the last few years, defense companies (including Lockheed and Boeing's defense business) have incurred multi-billion-dollar losses and charges on fixed-price development programs, but Lockheed recently outlined how the latest long-term agreements it made for PAC-3 missiles and F-35 fighter aircraft contain four key provisions that will help mitigate risk and encourage investment. It's a good sign, and if it continues, then defense stocks could rerate substantially.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By John Ballard – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:53AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Realty Income ›.

Realty Income (O +1.31%), a real estate investment trust (REIT) that leases properties to businesses, pays its dividend every month. After its Nov. 10 raise, the monthly dividend is $0.2740 per share, so 365 shares pay about $100 a month.

Industry observers note that at the Nov. 19 close of $57.66, it would take an investment of about $21,000 to earn that monthly income level at a dividend yield of about 5.7%.

NYSE · As of 11:39 AM ET 11/24/26.

According to recent reports, rent payments from triple net leases fund those dividends. The advantage of this structure is that tenants pay property taxes, insurance, and maintenance, which lowers the capital burden on Realty Income. At the end of September, its portfolio was 98.8% occupied, with an average lease term of about 8.5 years.

Importantly, about 90% of retail rent, which is the source of most of Realty's annual base rent, comes from "non-discretionary, service-oriented" businesses. This reflects management's strategy to lease space to tenants with strong business models that can generate a stable revenue stream through all market cycles.

Recent findings suggest that realty Income earns enough to cover the dividend with room to spare. In the third quarter, dividends used 73% of adjusted funds from operations (AFFO), a REIT's measure of cash earnings. The company has declared 677 consecutive monthly dividends and raised the payout for 117 straight quarters.

Higher interest rates are a headwind, making it more expensive for Realty Income to borrow money to buy upcoming properties. This can slow the growth of the cash it uses to pay dividends.

It has been revealed that still, Realty Income keeps buying properties that earn more than funding costs, and management just raised its outlook for this year. At about 13 times 2026 AFFO guidance and about 14% below its 52-week high, the stock offers long-term income investors an attractive entry point.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Aviation Administration said Monday it will investigate a recent Amazon drone crash near Detroit.

On Friday, one of Amazon's MK30 drones "landed on a resident's garage" during a delivery in Huntington Woods, Michigan, a suburb north of Detroit, Amazon spokesperson Jack Stelzner told CNBC in a statement.

In a recent development, the crash occurred after the drone dropped off a customer's shampoo order around 4:30 p.m. local time, and one of its propellers was damaged in the incident, according to ABC affiliate WXYZ.

A preliminary incident report posted to the FAA's website states the drone "struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff." The report says the condition of the drone is unknown.

Stelzner mentioned there were no injuries, the drone has been removed and Amazon is in contact with the resident.

In a recent development, "Safety is our top priority and incidents are extremely rare," Stelzner said. "Anytime a delivery does not go as planned we investigate what happened and use the findings to further improve the service.".

It has been revealed that an FAA spokesperson confirmed it's investigating the incident. A spokesperson for the National Transportation Safety Board, a federal agency that also investigates aviation accidents, said it's aware of the incident and is continuing to gather information. The agency hasn't yet determined whether it will open a probe, the NTSB spokesperson added.

Amazon has been working to make widespread drone delivery a reality ever since founder Jeff Bezos laid out his vision for the program nearly 13 years ago. The rollout has been slow, as the program encountered regulatory delays and staff cuts, as well as technical challenges and pushback from some communities where it conducted early pilots.

Expansion has recently ramped up. The company is targeting a launch of its drone service in 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of the year, while an Amazon executive claimed it has the "highest demand drone delivery service in the industry," CNBC previously reported.

The e-commerce giant has encountered some challenges along the way. Federal investigators opened a probe nearly one year ago after an Amazon drone downed an internet cable in Waco, Texas. One month earlier, a separate federal probe was opened into an incident near Phoenix, where two Amazon drones collided with a construction crane.

#176642. How Mykhailo Mudryk's unsolicited interview turned into a moany mess: With gaffes galore - including his Arsenal 'dream' - the £89m man hasn't endeared himself to either Spurs or Chelsea, writes KIERAN GILL

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1390 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

How Mykhailo Mudryk's unsolicited interview turned into a moany mess: With gaffes galore - including his Arsenal 'dream' - the £89m man hasn't endeared himself to either Spurs or Chelsea, writes KIERAN GILL

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1390 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:05 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:02 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • It has been revealed that not for the first time, Mykhailo Mudryk was in a good position, and displayed poor judgement.
  • Criticising London for its 20mph speed limit, saying 'it's hard to follow these rules, however much I'd like to' after his latest driving ban, and how the wealthy are taxed 45 per cent on these shores.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 07:05 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:02 EST, 20 November 2026.

It has been revealed that not for the first time, Mykhailo Mudryk was in a good position, and displayed poor judgement. This time, it was away from the pitch, in a two-hour, sit-down, tell-all interview involving gaffes galore.

Criticising London for its 20mph speed limit, saying 'it's hard to follow these rules, however much I'd like to' after his latest driving ban, and how the wealthy are taxed 45 per cent on these shores.

Naming 'Ukraine' when asked which is the best city in the world – he may have misunderstood the question, so we will let him off with that one – and admitting he signed contracts without reading them while denouncing the deals done by his former representatives.

Recent findings suggest that then there was his interviewer, a grinning chap called Dmitry Gordon, asking him if he speaks to his four cats in English, and why he wears earrings, and if girls send him pictures. Bizarre enquiries. Had Chelsea or Tottenham Hotspur known about this interview happening – and Daily Mail Sport understands they were not informed – then we cannot imagine either Premier League club would have liked such lines of questioning.

Recent findings suggest that nor will they, or their fanbases, be too fond of the 25-year-old Ukrainian explaining his move to England in the first place. He revealed how much he wanted to play for Arsenal, describing it as his 'dream' as he blamed his old agent for pushing him to Chelsea for the money.

What was supposed to be an opportunity for Mudryk to tell his side of the story, after a doping ban which cost him two years of his career, resembled more of a moany mess.

Mykhailo Mudryk's interview was a bizarre mess and showed his utter naivety.

The Ukrainian winger was given a one-year driving ban in December last year.

By the end, the seriousness of his allegations against the Ukrainian national team with regard to his failed drugs test were softened by the nonsensical own goals much more likely to set social media alight.

Such as the naivety of a Chelsea player on loan at Tottenham appearing to pine for Arsenal, and saying he still wants to win the Ballon d'Or, which is only ever an admission prone to being patronised online even if a sign of his ambition.

A reminder: Mudryk signed for Chelsea from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023 for £89million. He struggled, never looked like a winger worth such a fee. Frighteningly fast, but did not know how to use his weaponry properly in the Premier League. Graham Potter was his manager when he arrived. A few months later, it was Frank Lampard. A month after that, Mauricio Pochettino.

Then he was suspended for two years, during which time Chelsea supported his insistence that he was innocent and continued to pay his salary, believed to be worth around £100,000 per week.

While banned, he turned up in Wroclaw, Poland the day before the 2025 Conference League final, apparently there to collect his medal in case Chelsea won. Enzo Maresca was unaware, only learning that he was in the city when we told him at his pre-match press conference.

Upon Mudryk's return to football in the summer of 2026, Chelsea decided he needed to leave on loan, and another one of the Premier League's major-six sides gave him his second chance.

Tottenham called. Brentford, Brighton, Leeds and Coventry were among those also willing, but Roberto De Zerbi promised to give him a platform to prove his talents.

According to recent reports, he appeared once, as a 74th-minute substitute away at Nottingham Forest in September. Then he disappeared, injured, and his only sighting since has been here, on YouTube, as a 'Guest of Gordon'.

Chelsea will also be unhappy about Mudryk's interview and were not informed about it.

Mykhailo Mudryk's is still two weeks away from a Tottenham return after a suffering setback to his recovery from an ankle injury.

Mudryk, who has played only 16 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea, clashed with the Ukrainian FA this week when he blamed them for his positive drug test which ruled him out of football for almost two years.

He also risked the wrath of Spurs fans by admitting he only made the move across London to recover his fitness before returning to Stamford Bridge where Blues boss Xabi Alonso was 'counting on him'.

And he managed to annoy both Chelsea and Spurs fans by revealing, during the same YouTube interview, that he wanted to sign for Arsenal when he moved to the Premier League in January 2023 but his agent forced through the move with the best commission.

'I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy,' remarked Spurs boss De Zerbi, who worked with the Ukraine international at Shakhtar Dontetsk and convinced him to resist interest from Brentford and Coventry and be reunited in North London.

'He's a good player. He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he's playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a massive club, like the other clubs, not less at all.'.

Chelsea paid £86million for Mudryk but he made little impression before he was hit with a four-year ban in 2024, which was wiped out this summer enabling him to return to competition.

According to recent reports, 'He has no responsibility in this part,' noted De Zerbi. 'Now his focus is just on the ball or just on the football. He has a significant chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club. He knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play.

In a recent development, 'He knows I give him total confidence to show what he is. So to move the focus in the right direction, in a good direction. But I think he's working hard to recover and to play earlier.'.

Mudryk made his Spurs debut as a sub at Nottingham Forest in September but injured an ankle in training a few days later. He was initially expected to be out for two months with Saturday's game against Ipswich his target to return.

Recent findings suggest that 'The plan was to be available for Ipswich or Sunderland,' noted De Zerbi, who will serve a touchline ban against Ipswich for three yellow cards. 'Then he felt not pain but he was not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we're going to see the situation.'.

While there should be sympathy with Mudryk, who had to bite his tongue while banned and spending what he described as 'millions' on trying to clear his name, he made a poor choice in the platform chosen to finally speak up.

At one stage, he is asked bluntly whether he considered killing himself. 'No, that's not a way out,' he replied. The title of the video on YouTube, unhelpfully, mentions 'suicidal thoughts' regardless of his answer.

Mudryk may have thought it would help to talk so openly, especially to clarify those he holds responsible for the two years he lost as a footballer.

But he hardly endeared himself to his current club, Tottenham, or to his parent club, Chelsea, to whom he is still contracted into the 2030s.

He likened them to chaos, explaining: 'I came to a Chelsea that was, and perhaps still is, in the middle of a rebuild. It's not the Chelsea that existed under the previous owners, which was stable, had a clear system, coaches, without this constant galloping who knows where.'.

Such comments are unlikely to be well received when read by the club's hierarchy, while he also noted on Chelsea's managerial merry-go-round: 'The coaches themselves don't know what tactics they'll play. They come to the club and try one set of tactics. Whether it works or not, they try another.'.

According to recent reports, when Mudryk returns from his ankle injury, he will have to hope his football can do the talking. After this, neither Tottenham nor Chelsea are likely to want him to speak again any time soon.

#176635. Latest Update: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📅 30 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 24m • 📚 Deep Dive (4898 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

📅 30 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • It has been revealed that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • In a recent development, but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

It has been revealed that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

In a recent development, but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that “The data is not important,” Alonso stated. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Industry observers note that jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

Sources indicate that “After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso noted. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

In a recent development, it is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

Industry observers note that “I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez mentioned. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

Industry observers note that conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Industry observers note that caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was rapidly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

It has been revealed that “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Sources indicate that macPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

It has been revealed that fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they highlighted it in certain moments of the game.”.

Sources indicate that palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro notes he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

According to recent reports, 6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

The final game of the day comes from the north west as Manchester United host newly-promoted Ipswich. That game kicks off at 4.30pm and you can follow all the live action from that match right here.

Recent findings suggest that there is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Recent findings suggest that brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

Chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

How many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

In a recent development, this is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Industry observers note that tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:.

In a recent development, dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

According to recent reports, chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

It has been revealed that xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

According to recent reports, it is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

It has been revealed that this game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a major deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

Recent findings suggest that we are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

But it is the intangibles that set Martínez apart and why his availability at a knock-down price from Aston Villa convinced Chelsea to seize a market opportunity.

At £7.5m, Martínez could prove to be Chelsea’s smartest piece of business of the summer and there is little doubt he will be box-office at Stamford Bridge.
